app.text: The tab bar has five tabs: Home, Calculators, More, Records and Ask. Home: what's in progress, Needs Attention, Start work (New Run, Quick Run, Confined Space Permit, + New), My production and My inspections & tests (foremen), and My Shortcuts. Calculators: every calculator, grouped (Grade & Elevation, Trench & Backfill, Pipe & Flow, Structures, Confined Space). More (it used to be called Tools): search box "Search tools and calculators", Toolbox Talks, Education & Reference, Stats, Job Summary, Confined Space Reference and the rest. Records: finished paperwork (runs, permits, dailies, tickets, management reports) in one list. Ask: questions about the app or the trade; it opens over the screen you're on, so nothing you're filling in is lost. On a wide screen (tablet, 1024 px and up) the tabs become a left sidebar.
app.title: The bottom tabs: Home, Calculators, More, Records, Ask

app.text: Access is a ladder: pipelayer, then foreman, then superintendent / project manager, then the company account. Each step has everything the step below has plus its own. Pipelayer: runs, Quick Run, calculators, confined space permits, field tickets, management reports, sending run reports. Foreman: all of that plus his crew (approving run reports, entering production, Crew & Equipment Log), the daily report, inspections check-off, locates, work without a run, the job book and toolbox talk schedule. Super and PM have the same account (only the title differs): all foreman access as a fallback when a foreman doesn't finish a run review, plus jobs, plans, materials, equipment, schedules, crew members, inspections setup and the company dashboards. The company (owner) account has everything, including billing, making PMs and deleting jobs. Foremen can't edit job plans. The company account has no crew row, so it has no My production.
app.title: Who can do what (pipelayer, foreman, super/PM, company)

app.text: Field Home (pipelayer, foreman): Current job (tap Choose › to pick it), then for a foreman Add note and Daily report, the My crew now tiles (active runs, active permits), Run reports to approve, Permits closed, On my crew (Add or remove crew). Then Current Work (Continue Run, Finish Run, Open Active Permit, Continue Draft, Run ended), Needs Attention cards, My production and My inspections & tests (foremen), Start work (New Run, Quick Run, Confined Space Permit, New) and My Shortcuts. Company Home (company account, PMs, supers) shows Live now, Management inbox, Material alert, Waiting on foremen, New run report and Delays & extra work tiles, then every job with its % complete, then New record, Company production, Company tickets, Company inspections & tests, My production / My inspections & tests links, and Field tools (New run, Quick Run, permits, shortcuts, folded). An open permit or emergency always shows on Home.
app.title: Home screen: what each part is

app.text: Where: Home › Current job › Choose ›. Steps: tap it, pick a job from the list (your company's jobs, then jobs from runs and permits on this phone) or type a number under "Or type a job number" and tap Use It. Clear Current Job removes it. What it does: new runs start on that job (Job details turned on with its number), a new permit's Job number fills in from it (marked auto until you type over it), Add note and the Daily report use it, the job book opens on it and toolbox talks are marked on it. It is kept per account on this phone. You must be signed in. The company Home has no Current job card.
app.title: Pick the Current job

app.text: Where: Home › Start work › New (on Company Home: New record). The sheet lists what your account can start: Field ticket, Work without a run (foremen and up), Job book entry (foremen), Management report (pipelayers and foremen; the office receives reports instead of sending them). A foreman's Daily report is the button under Current job on Home, not in this sheet. Back from what you open returns to Home. Records is for finished paperwork; everything you start is on Home.
app.title: + New: start a record from Home

app.text: Where: any calculator or tool screen › Add to Home, or Home › My Shortcuts › Edit. Edit Shortcuts shows On Home (the order they appear) and Add a shortcut with a search box ("Search tools and actions"). Tap Save (or Save now) to keep it, Cancel to drop changes, Restore Default Shortcuts to go back to the starting set (Material Volume, Trench Sloping, Tenths ↔ Inches, Structure Bedding). Removing a shortcut only removes the link; the tool and your records stay. Show all opens the full list when there are many.
app.title: My Shortcuts on Home (add, remove, reorder)

app.text: Where: More tab › Search tools and calculators. Type a word (volume, grade, trench, permit, stats) and tap the result. The same search is in Edit Shortcuts ("Search tools and actions"). Education & Reference has its own search box ("What are you trying to understand?") for lessons and reference pages.
app.title: Search for a tool or calculator

app.text: Where: Home › Log In (or Account and settings › Log In). Enter Email and Password and tap Log In. Forgot password? opens a box with your email filled in; tap Send Reset Link and open the email with signal (check spam). Setting the new password ends signed out: you log in again with the new one. Log Out is in Account & Settings; it asks first about work that hasn't saved, and everything already saved on this phone stays. After a session expires, the Log In box keeps your last email.
app.title: Log in, log out, forgot password

app.text: Where: Home › your profile button (top right) or Account and settings at the bottom of Home. Rows: Account (who's signed in and the plan), Name (Edit › Save Name), What each plan includes, Log In / Log Out, Company (Crew members, Company logo, Time zone, Company equipment: office only), Appearance (Auto / Light / Dark), Text size (Normal / Large / Extra Large), Push notifications, Send crash reports, Report an App Problem, and Copy app version.
app.title: Account & Settings: what's in it

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Name › Edit. Type Your name and tap Save Name (Cancel to stop). Your company sees this name instead of your email, unless the company set a name for you in Crew members. The app also asks once on the first sign-in after joining a company; you can skip it. Names are plain text, one line, up to 80 characters.
app.title: Set your name

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Appearance: Auto, Light or Dark. Auto (the default) follows the phone's own light/dark setting. Text size: Normal, Large or Extra Large; the change shows the moment you tap it. Both are kept on this phone.
app.title: Light mode, dark mode and text size

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Company › Time zone › Edit (company account, PMs and supers). Pick the zone and tap Save. Alerts, quiet hours, the 811 and daily-report days and the 6:00 AM morning email follow it. Until it is set, alerts follow the zone shown and a Needs Attention card asks the office to set it (Choose Time Zone). The owner also sees "Send my own copies to this account" (off by default).
app.title: Company time zone and morning email

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Company logo. Tap Upload Logo, pick a PNG, JPEG or SVG up to 2 MB, check the preview and tap Save Logo (Cancel to drop it). Remove Logo takes it off; reports already saved or sent don't change. The logo prints at the top of every company report; without one the company name prints in bold. Needs signal. Company account, PMs and supers.
app.title: Company logo on reports

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Report an App Problem. Fill in What happened?, optionally What did you expect to happen? and Which screen?, and tap Send to App Owner. It goes to the person who makes the app, not your company. The app version and screen are attached; your runs, permits, photos and password never are. With no signal it is saved on this phone and goes by itself next time this account is signed in with signal. Not for safety or workplace problems: use Management report.
app.title: Report an App Problem

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Send crash reports (switch). On, the phone sends a short error report when something in the app breaks, so it can be fixed. "What crash reports send" explains exactly what goes; no records, names or readings. Send a test report checks it works.
app.title: Crash reports

app.text: When a company adds your email in Crew members, an existing account gets an in-app invitation on Home and in Settings. Tap Accept to join (or Decline). Until you accept you are not a member and not a seat. A new email gets an invite link by email. One account can belong to more than one company.
app.title: Accept an invitation to a company

app.text: Where: Home › Start work › New Run (Company Home: Field tools › New Run). Run Setup steps: 1 Job & Pipe: Job number (required for company crews) and Jobsite (from the Current job), Foreman (company pipelayers pick the foreman the report goes to; pre-filled with the most recent pick or the foreman who claimed you), Pipe type (fills wall thickness and laying length, marked auto), rod (Lenker Rod, Engineer's Rod, Architect's Rod), Wall thickness (ft) (required), Pipe ID (inches), and Bedding, Shading & Materials. 2 Points & Instrument: Height of Instrument (Calculate from Stakes, Benchmark + Backsight, or I know my HI), Start Point (station, invert or rod reading, optional label and photos), Hubs (optional, + Add Hub), End Point (by Station or Distance), Interval (ft). Then tap Review & Calculate. Cancel at the top leaves without making anything (it asks first if you typed). Import Cutsheet fills the points from a cutsheet; Reuse Pipe Settings copies pipe settings from a locked run on this phone (not points or hubs).
app.title: Start a new run (Run Setup)

app.text: Where: New Run › Run Setup › Import Cutsheet. Tap Add Cutsheet and pick a PDF or photo, or open "Paste rows instead", paste the rows and tap Parse Rows. Check the rows you want (Check a stake range: From / To Stake #, Check This Range, Uncheck All), then tap Import Checked Rows as This Run. If the run reads backwards the app asks to flip it (Yes, Flip It / No, Keep As Is). Rows from more than one pipe are split into groups you pick with tabs. After import, check Wall thickness and Pipe ID (they aren't on the sheet). Readable PDFs and pasted rows stay on the phone; a scan or photo goes to AI (Anthropic) only after you agree. Numbers need a decimal point (2394.00), feet-inches aren't read. Importing replaces what was already typed for this run.
app.title: Add a cutsheet to a run (Import From Cutsheet)

app.text: Where: Run Setup › 2 Points & Instrument › Hubs (optional) › + Add Hub. Each hub has a station (or distance) and readings. A hub can be a Fitting: pick Fitting (Bend, Tee, Wye, Reducer, Coupling, Other), Size / angle, and Laying length (ft); the laying length fills in from the app's fitting table for the pipe type (marked auto; type over it to change it). The hub station is the fitting's center: pipe going in stops half the laying length before it, pipe coming out starts half after. Grades and elevations don't change. + Add Crossing records a crossing utility (station, its INV / BOP / TOP, OD, min. clearance, default 12 in) and checks your pipe clears it. Collapse All / Expand All fold the hub cards.
app.title: Hubs, fittings and crossings on Run Setup

app.text: Where: Run Setup › The Run › Add Additional Run. Use it for a reducer or a change in pipe on the same instrument setup (same HI only; if you moved the instrument, lock this run and start a New Run). Run 2 gets its own Start Point, hubs, End Point, interval, wall thickness, pipe ID, bedding and trench width. Measured step (ft) at the reducer is optional: + if Run 2 sits higher, − if lower, measured bell bottom to bell bottom (bottom of pipe, not invert); or type Run 2's start invert at its Start Point instead. Up to five runs. Remove Run 2 takes it off.
app.title: Pipe size changes partway (Add Additional Run)

app.text: Where: Run Setup › Review & Calculate. The Check Before Locking screen shows the numbers and any warnings (each with a Details fold): backflow ("Invert falls from Start to End" with Flip This Run), Deep Trench - Check Sloping, intervals, crossings. Tap Go Back & Fix to change something, or Lock This Run. If the run has no job number the app asks Which Job Is This Run On? (pick a company job or type one). A company pipelayer with no foreman picked is asked once (Pick / Lock anyway); the report then waits for a foreman. If this same form already locked a run and you changed it, it asks Replace / Keep Both / Cancel. After Lock, Run Results opens and the run is saved in Records on this phone.
app.title: Lock a run (Review & Calculate, Check Before Locking)

app.text: Where: after Lock, or Home › Continue Run. Top: Run details, Columns, Hide laid, Zoom and End Run?. The grade rows show station, BOP, INV, TOP and cut/fill; each row's ⋯ menu has Mark laid to here and the calculators (Bend Offset, Structure Bedding, Trench Sloping, Rod Reading). Below: Adjust pipe layout (Adjust First Pipe, Adjust at a Station), Run Notes (Delay, Utility Found, Rework, Equipment), Edit Run Data, Production & Crew (foremen and individual accounts), Finish this run (End Run and Send Report / End Run, End Run Without Completing, Adjust End Time), More (Correct a Distance or Hub, Add Interval, Change Spacing), View Report and Save PDF. A company pipelayer sees "Production and crew hours are entered by your foreman" instead of Production & Crew.
app.title: Run Results screen: the buttons

app.text: Where: Run Results grade rows. Swipe right across a row to mark it laid; swipe back to undo. Marking a later row also marks every earlier row with the same time; undoing a row undoes it and every later one, so "laid to here" is one point. No swipe? Use the row's ⋯ menu › Mark laid to here / Undo laid from here. Laid rows show "Laid 10:42"; the next row gets a Next tag; Hide laid folds them. Marks feed the progress line ("Pipe laid: 120 of 400 ft"), the foreman's live crew view and the pre-filled Feet of pipe installed. Locked and ended runs can still be marked; it never changes grades.
app.title: Mark pipe laid (laid to here)

app.text: Where: Run Results › More › Change Spacing. Pick Which run?, type Pipe laying length (ft) (filled from the pipe type when the table has it: PVC SDR 35 14 ft, C900 and ductile iron 20 ft, concrete 8 ft, corrugated HDPE 20 ft), tick Use laying length for intervals, pick Divide each stick (Joints only, Halves, Quarters), add an optional Reason and tap Apply Spacing. The rows then fall on the pipe joints.
app.title: Pipe laying length and row spacing (Change Spacing)

app.text: Where: Run Results › Adjust pipe layout › Adjust First Pipe or Adjust at a Station (or a row's Adjust Pipe Layout Here). Type the Station where this pipe starts, choose Enter it as: Actual installed length or Length cut off a full stick, type the length, an optional Reason (e.g. cut to fit at the manhole), and tap Apply Adjustment. The joints after it move to match. Grades don't change.
app.title: Adjust the pipe layout (first pipe, cut stick)

app.text: Where: Run Results › More. Correct a Distance or Hub: pick What are you correcting?, type the Actual distance (ft) or the hub Station, an optional Reason, and tap Apply Correction (it resets the run to Not Sent; the history keeps the original). Add Interval: type Station (ft from start) and an optional Label (e.g. service tap), tap Add This Interval. Edit Run Data reopens Run Setup with the run for bigger changes; locking it again replaces that record.
app.title: Correct a distance or hub, add an interval

app.text: Where: Run Results › Run Notes. Tap Delay, Utility Found, Rework or Equipment, fill it in, tap Save Entry. Delay: Reason (Utility conflict, Waiting on inspector, Weather, Equipment down, Waiting on material, Waiting on survey / stakes, Traffic control, Other), Start and End, or "Or the hours lost", Note. Utility Found: What was hit or found (Water, Gas, Electric, Telecom, Sewer, Storm, Abandoned line, Unknown), Station (grade row), Damaged?, Who was notified, Note, photos. Rework: From / To station, Reason (Grade off, Damaged pipe, Failed test, Inspector call, Other), Hours. Equipment: Machine (from the crew log or typed), Hours (Use crew log hours), Breakdown?, Downtime. Entries keep the time, zone and who; an edit keeps the old version. They go to the company as their own records, and every Delay flows into that day's daily report automatically.
app.title: Run Notes: delay, utility found, rework, equipment

app.text: Where: Run Results › Run Notes › Equipment. Pick the Machine, set Breakdown? to "Yes, it broke down", type Downtime, hours, and tap Save Entry. The app then asks "Machine broke down. Crew stopped too?" with Add a Delay. One tap opens the run's Delay entry with Equipment down picked, the start set to now and the machine in the note; finish the hours/end time and Save Entry. Nothing is saved until you save it. That delay then shows on the day's daily report under Delays & Extra Work. Foremen entering Down hours on My crew production get the same Add a Delay button.
app.title: Equipment breaks down during a run (Add a Delay)

app.text: Where: Run Results › Production & Crew (foremen, PMs, supers, the company and individual accounts; never a company pipelayer). Enter Production: Entered by (foreman name), Feet excavated, Feet of pipe installed (pre-filled from laid marks), Feet of backfill completed, Feet of restoration completed, Feet of demo completed, Number of appurtenances, then Save Production. Quantities are today's work for this run session, not a running total. It is saved on the phone and synced to the company (it counts toward the job's categories); the foreman's production is the crew's production, never counted twice.
app.title: Production & Crew on your own run (enter production)

app.text: Where: Run Results › Production & Crew › + Add Laborer, Operator, or Equipment. Type Name / Equipment, pick Type (Laborer, Operator, Equipment; equipment can be marked Rental) and Category (Excavation, Pipe Installation, Backfill, Restoration, General/Other), then Add or Add and Check In. Check people out when they leave; someone switching category gets a second entry. Closed hours feed the crew hours, the daily report's Crew Today and Equipment on Site, and the job's budget-hours pace. Ending a run with someone still checked in asks you to check them out (Check Them Out Now).
app.title: Crew & Equipment Log (check people and machines in and out)

app.text: Where: Run Results › Finish this run. Company crews see End Run and Send Report; others see End Run. Ending marks the run finished, stops its clock and (company crews) sends the run report in the app to the foreman picked on Run Setup and the office copy, as soon as there's signal. No foreman picked: it goes to the office and waits until a foreman takes it. Home then shows "Run ended" with View Report and Save PDF, and "Report sent to <foreman> and the office · time" (or "Report saved on this phone: it goes … as soon as there's signal"). You can add a closing note for the foreman (Add a note for …, up to 140 characters). A report never sent is sent automatically 12 hours after the run ended.
app.title: End a run and send its report

app.text: Where: Run Results › Finish this run › End Run Without Completing. Pick Stopped at which interval? (the furthest row marked laid is suggested) and tap Confirm — End Here (Cancel to go back). Footage, backfill and bedding are figured to the stop point. The run shows on Home as Finish Run ("Ended early at …") so you can pick it up later, and its report is sent like a normal end.
app.title: End a run early (End Run Without Completing)

app.text: Where: Home › Finish Run (a run ended early) or Home › Continue Run (a locked run still open). Finish Run opens Resume This Run: a new session for today with one fresh rod reading; the earlier part stays in its own record. A run left open overnight asks first Where Did This Run End? (pick the grade row and the time work stopped); a point short of the end then offers Continue Today. Not Now goes Home and asks again later. The individual plan finishes from Home the same way. Records › On this phone also has Resume This Run.
app.title: Resume a run you didn't finish

app.text: Where: Run Results › Finish this run › Adjust End Time (after the run is ended), or Records › On this phone › the run › More actions › Adjust End Time. Pick the real stop time and save. The report says the end was entered later. Foremen can adjust a run's end time after it is ended.
app.title: Adjust a run's end time

app.text: A run typed into Run Setup but not locked is kept as a draft on this phone. Home shows Continue Draft; tap it to go back. Starting a New Run with a draft asks Continue That Run or Start New (discards it). Each account keeps several drafts. A draft is never a record and never goes to Records, Stats or the company. Photos aren't kept in drafts.
app.title: Continue a draft run (not locked yet)

app.text: Where: Home › Start work › Quick Run. Pick the rod (Lenker Rod, Engineer's Rod, Architect's Rod), then enter three of the four values: Reading at Start, Reading at End, Slope (%) and Distance (ft). The fourth is calculated and marked Calculated (type over it to change it). Fall is positive: + means the pipe drops from start to end (full runs use rise-positive). Row spacing (ft) sets the table interval (blank = 10 ft). Nothing goes to Records, Stats or management; what you enter is kept on this phone until you tap Clear Calculation.
app.title: Quick Run (grade math only)

app.text: Where: Run Results › View Report / Save PDF, Home › Run ended card, or Records (tap the run). View opens the in-app PDF viewer: zoom (100 / 150 / 200 %), Download, Share (on phones that can), Text version. On an iPhone Home Screen app the PDF goes to the share sheet (Save to Files, Mail, Print). The individual plan uses Save to Phone on Results. "Sent" means sent in the app; emailing a copy is separate (Records › Email a Copy).
app.title: View, save or share a run report

app.text: Where: Home › Run reports to approve (the tile counts what's waiting "From your crew"). Tap a report: it shows the summary (start, end, footage, laid, photos, notes, the pipelayer's closing note) and the production form. Enter what the crew did on this run (categories, Crew hours, Equipment hours: Used h / Idle h / Down h per piece) and tap Approve Report. With nothing typed it asks Approve Without Production (nothing counts). If the pipelayer entered his own numbers, use Approve as Mine (they become your entry) or Already Counted. The list also holds Changes to approve and "Ended runs, report not here yet". The pipelayer then sees "<you> approved your report · time" on Home.
app.title: Approve a crew run report (foreman)

app.text: Who: the office (company account, PMs, supers), or a foreman who is also a listed manager. Where: the run report (Company Home › New run report or Waiting on foremen › Run reports). Tap Send Back to Foreman, type What does the foreman need to add or fix? (up to 500 characters) and tap Send Back. The pipelayer gets a Home card "<name> sent back your run …: <reason>" and a push (Run reports sent back), and the foreman is told. The pipelayer taps Fix It, which opens the run's data; after Review & Calculate and Lock the same report is corrected (never a second report) and goes back up. The foreman and whoever sent it back are told it was corrected.
app.title: Send back a run report

app.text: Where: Home › the "sent back your run" card, or the Sent Back dialog. Tap Fix It (View Report shows it first, Not Now waits). Fix It opens Edit Run Data for that run; change what was asked, tap Review & Calculate, then Lock This Run. The same report is corrected in place (notes, laid marks, crew log and end are kept) and goes back to the foreman / office. If another run is still open, end it first. Records shows "Corrected · waiting" until it is approved.
app.title: Fix a run report that was sent back (pipelayer)

app.text: When a foreman doesn't review a run report, the office can finish it. Where: Company Home › New run report or Waiting on foremen › the run report (or the job page › Waiting tab). The report says "Waiting for <foreman> to enter production". Under More: Enter Production (enter it yourself) or Approve Report (approve as it is). With production already entered: Correct Production (the foreman sees who changed it). After your own Send Back with no answer: Approve Without <foreman> (asks first and the foreman sees you approved it). Lists cover the last 60 days; photos stay on the crew's phone.
app.title: Supers and PMs step in on a run review

app.text: A run's production entered by a pipelayer is held for a foreman for 24 hours. Pipelayer: My production › Runs waiting for a foreman › Assign to a Foreman (or Assign to Another Foreman) or Send to the Company. The assigned foreman (any foreman if none) can Approve as Mine (it becomes his editable entry) or Already Counted. If nobody acts in 24 hours it counts on its own, noted "Counted: not claimed by a foreman within 24 hours". The office sees these under Waiting on foremen and can Nudge Pipelayer / the foreman.
app.title: Pipelayer runs waiting for a foreman (24-hour hold)

app.text: When someone changes production that already counted, the earlier numbers keep counting until it's approved. Where: foreman: Home › Run reports to approve › Changes to approve; office: Company Home › Waiting on foremen or the job page › Waiting tab › Waiting for your approval. Each shows "Pipe Installed: 80 LF → 95 LF, by <name>"; tap Approve or Reject. The pipelayer sees "Your change is waiting for approval" until then.
app.title: Approve or reject a change to production

app.text: Runs ended on an older version, or ended with no signal, show on Home as Send Run Report ("Not sent. Sends itself 12 h after the run ended."). Tap it, then Send Report (View Report to check first, Not Now to wait). It goes to the run's foreman and the office as soon as there's signal. A report the server refuses for good says why on Home and in Records (for example the account isn't in a company: save a PDF and hand it over).
app.title: Send a run report that didn't go (Send Run Report)

app.text: Where: Home › On my crew (Add or remove crew), or Home › My production › My crew. Tap Add to My Crew and pick from your company's current pipelayers (someone with another foreman moves to you). Remove takes them off; production you already entered stays. A pipelayer's runs come to you automatically once they're on your crew. The company never sets pairings; foremen and pipelayers do.
app.title: Add or remove pipelayers on your crew (foreman)

app.text: Two places. On each run: Run Setup › Foreman (the run report goes to that foreman; pre-filled with your last pick or the foreman who claimed you). For your crew link: Home › My production › My foreman › Pick My Foreman (Change Foreman, or No Foreman to leave). Typing a foreman on a run also puts you on that foreman's crew. With no foreman, reports go to the office and wait.
app.title: Pick your foreman (pipelayer)

app.text: Where: Home › My crew now tiles, or My production › My crew now. Shows each linked pipelayer's current run (job, run, how far laid, last laid row, last update) and today's runs, as the phone last reported them. Tap Enter production for this run to enter the crew's production from your phone while the run is still going or after it ends (Crew hours, Equipment hours with Used / Idle / Down, Job number if the run has none), then Save Production. If a piece has Down hours, Add a Delay opens today's daily report with a delay entry filled in. Open Run Report opens a sent report.
app.title: My crew now: your pipelayers' live runs (foreman)

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Crew members. Add crew member: Email, Name (optional), Role (Foreman or Pipelayer; the owner also sees Project manager and Superintendent), then Add Crew Member. An existing account gets an in-app invitation to accept; a new email gets an invite. In Your crew each person has Edit Name, Make Foreman / Make Pipelayer, Make Project Manager / Make Superintendent, Remove from Company, Resend Invite or Withdraw Invitation. PMs and supers can rename people, switch PM↔Super and take PMs off jobs; only the owner makes or changes managers and handles billing. Needs signal. The member count vs your plan's seats shows at the top.
app.title: Add and manage crew members (company, PMs, supers)

app.text: Where: on a Needs Attention card's ⋯ menu, a locates card, your runs-waiting card, a run report waiting for approval, or the office's material alerts list: Nudge your foreman / Nudge super / PM / Nudge the owner. The server picks who hears: pipelayer → his foreman, foreman → the job's supers/PMs, super/PM → the company account, and sends a push. With no signal the nudge waits on the phone and goes when there's signal. The person nudged sees a Home card they can mark Handled or pass on up.
app.title: Nudge someone up the chain

app.text: Where: Home › Daily report (under Current job), or a Needs Attention card for a day not done. Two tabs: Notes (Narrative of the day, quick notes with Add Note, photos) and Report (every section, signing at the bottom). Report sections fill themselves: Weather, Runs & Production, Materials, Inspections & Tests, Confined Space Permits, Other Crews' Production, Crew Today and Equipment on Site (from the day's runs and crew log; change hours or add names), Delays & Extra Work, Attached Reports (Attach to the PDF switch, on by default), Toolbox Talks. To sign: Your full name, an optional drawn signature (Clear Signature to redo), Sign Report, then confirm Sign This Report? › Sign Report. Save for Later keeps it on the phone. Pick any earlier Report date for a missed day.
app.title: Write and sign the daily report (foreman)

app.text: Signing locks the report (corrections go in as amendments). It goes to the company server with your name and time, as a PDF with the day's run reports and permits attached; crew reports not sent yet attach once they arrive ("Added after signing"). PMs, supers and the company read it under Records › Dailies and the job's Inspections & daily reports. Each delay, standby or extra-work entry goes to the job's PMs and the company account (push "Delays & extra work") and to the office's Delays & extra work list. Tomorrow's report starts with today's crew and equipment. To fix it later: Add an Amendment.
app.title: What happens after you sign a daily

app.text: Where: Home › Add note (foremen). A sheet opens on today's daily for the Current job (or asks the Job number): type the note, Add Photo if you want, set an optional Reminder (None, In 1 hour, End of day, Tomorrow 7:00 AM, Pick a time…) and tap Save. It's added to that day's daily Notes without opening it. A reminder pushes to you at that time.
app.title: Add a quick note to today's daily (Add note)

app.text: Where: Daily report › Report › Delays & Extra Work › Add an Entry. New entry: pick Delay, Standby or Extra work; Reason (Weather, Utility conflict, Waiting on inspector, Waiting on materials, Design change, Owner-directed, Other); Detail (what happened, who asked for it, where); Hours (more than 0, at most 24); Crew size; Equipment idle (tick pieces on site); photos; then Add Entry (Cancel to drop). Change / Remove edit it before signing. At most 40 entries per report. Run Notes delays from the day's runs show here automatically as "from runs" rows, with Change (make it your own entry) or Same as Mine (link it to an entry you already made) so each delay counts once. After signing, the job's PMs and the company get a push and it shows in their Delays & extra work list.
app.title: Add a delay, standby or extra work entry

app.text: Where: Company Home › Delays & extra work tile (or the job page Overview line). It lists every delay, standby and extra work entry from foremen's signed daily reports, last 30 days, including delays that came from Run Notes. On each: Mark Reviewed, T&M Ticket Sent, or Back to New. Your marks are saved on the phone and sent with signal. A push "Delays & extra work" comes when a foreman signs a daily with one (Settings › Push notifications).
app.title: Review delays and extra work (office)

app.text: Both fill themselves from the day's run reports (your runs and your crew's sent reports): people and machines from the Crew & Equipment Log, overlapping time counted once, plus Run Notes equipment hours. Each filled line has a "from runs" tag. Change the hours (it's then yours and never overwritten) or remove a line. Add a name / Add equipment adds people not on the app or pieces (pick from company equipment or type; tick Rental for rentals). On a new day the lists start from your last report. Still-checked-in people aren't counted until checked out.
app.title: Crew Today and Equipment on Site on the daily

app.text: The daily report's Weather comes from the National Weather Service for the job's City, State. If the job has none: type City, State and tap Set Location, or Use Phone Location Once. The office sets a job's City, State in job setup (Edit project › Job details). Check Again appears once the job has a location.
app.title: Weather on the daily report

app.text: Where: Daily report (signed) › Add an Amendment. It opens a copy of the signed version to change; sign it again. The company keeps every version (v1, v2 …) and the PDF says which. Signed reports themselves can't be changed.
app.title: Amend a signed daily report

app.text: A foreman's Home shows "Not done" under the Daily report button with the past days (last 14) that had work and no signed daily; tap it to pick a day and write it. Supers and PMs stepping in to fill in and sign a day the foreman missed (Needs Attention "Daily report not signed", + New › Daily report, "Filling in for <foreman>") is coming with a server update; until then the office reads dailies and nudges the foreman.
app.title: When a foreman doesn't sign a daily

app.text: Where: Home › New › Field ticket (or Home › My production › Field tickets › New Ticket). Pick the type: Concrete, Material or Sub. Take Photo of the ticket, then Read Ticket With AI to fill it in, or type it: Supplier / Company (sub), Ticket #, Date, Time; concrete adds Truck, Mix design, Yards (yd³), PSI, Slump, Admixtures, Water added (gal); material has Items (Add Item: item, qty, unit); sub has Hours, Crew, Equipment. Then Job number, Jobsite, Cost code, Cost code name (optional), Use (concrete) and Notes / caption, and tap Save Ticket. Everyone can file tickets, the company account too.
app.title: File a field ticket (concrete, material, sub)

app.text: It's saved on this phone first ("Not synced yet") and sent to the company when there's signal; the original photo goes too. It shows on Company tickets (totals by mix, use, cost code, item and sub hours) and counts toward the job's matching material automatically. Concrete and asphalt tickets count as used, not ordered (they aren't stockpiled). A line the app can't match shows "Not assigned to a material" for the PM. There's no approval step; tickets show management what will be billed.
app.title: What happens to a field ticket after you save it

app.text: On a concrete ticket, Use says what it went into: Encasement, Thrust blocks, Collars, Manhole base / bench, Pipe bedding (CLSM), Backfill (flowable fill), Curb / sidewalk / paving restoration, or Other (type it). It fills itself (with an auto pill): the job plan's only concrete material when there's exactly one, otherwise the last Use picked on that job. Your pick is never overwritten. Use and mix show as totals on Company tickets.
app.title: Concrete ticket Use (what the concrete was for)

app.text: Where: Field ticket › Take Photo › Read Ticket With AI. The photo goes through the app's server to Anthropic to be read (not stored by the app); the fields fill in for you to check before Save Ticket. Needs signal and a paid plan. View Original Photo shows the picture. Don't use AI with confidential project info.
app.title: Read a ticket with AI

app.text: Where: Company Home › Company tickets. Pick a Job (or All jobs). Shows ticket count, concrete yd³, Concrete by mix, Concrete by use, By cost code, Materials by item, Sub hours by company, then each ticket (View opens it). Refresh / Load Older. Field crews see their own tickets in Records › Tickets.
app.title: Company tickets page (office)

app.text: Where: Home › Start work › Confined Space Permit (or More › Confined Space Permits › New Entry Permit). Fill the six sections: 1 Location & Work (Jobsite, Job number, Site address you'd give 911, Entrance location, Space identification, Purpose), 2 Permit Window (date, authorized start and end time; end date fills itself), 3 People & Communication (Entry supervisor name and initials, Attendant, communication procedures, comm check reminder), 4 Hazards & Controls (hazard checkboxes with explanations, isolation, ventilation-failure detection, gas limits, air test re-check reminder, equipment), 5 Rescue & Emergency Plan (Emergency number, default 911; rescue services; optional second contact), 6 Notes & Photos. Reuse Last Permit's Hazards & Controls fills the hazards, limits, rescue and emergency info from the last permit. Tap Review Permit, then Lock & Activate Permit. Locking records the time as authorization; after that only the EMERGENCY number can be changed.
app.title: Open a confined space entry permit

app.text: Every air test is checked against the permit's limits; one outside them sounds EVACUATE and shows DO NOT ENTER. Blank fields use the standard values: O2 minimum 19.5%, O2 maximum 23.5% (oxygen-enriched air is a fire hazard), LEL maximum 10%, H2S maximum 10 ppm (OSHA construction limit, 8-hour average), CO maximum 25 ppm (the Cal/OSHA limit, lower than federal OSHA and NIOSH; NIOSH recommends 35 and federal OSHA allows 50). H2S and CO readings are optional; a blank reading means not measured, never zero. Keep using your gas meter's own alarm.
app.title: Gas limits the permit checks

app.text: Where: Active Permit › Log Air Test (or + Log Air Test / + Add Test Reading). Type O2 (%), LEL (%), H2S (ppm, optional), CO (ppm, optional), Other contaminant reading (optional), Tester name, and tap Save Reading. The newest reading is checked at once; a bad one sounds EVACUATE. The Air test re-check reminder (minutes) set on the permit reminds you to test again and sets how old the last test can be before check-in is blocked (20 minutes when blank). Set reminder starts a repeating reminder later. Reminders run while the screen is open and awake; Permit checks due also pushes when the phone is locked (Settings › Push notifications).
app.title: Log gas readings (air tests)

app.text: Where: Active Permit › Manage Roster › + Add Person. Type Name, pick Role (Entrant, Attendant, Entry Supervisor), tap Add to Roster. Each person has Check In / Check Out; the attendant has Reassign Attendant. Check-in is blocked while readings are unsafe, the last air test is too old, or an emergency is open: the app shows DO NOT ENTER and asks whether the person entered anyway, and logs it ("ENTERED AGAINST BLOCK"). Log Communication Check (+ Log Check) records routine check-ins; View Full Log shows everything.
app.title: Roster: check entrants in and out

app.text: Where: the red EMERGENCY button at the top of Active Permit. It opens the phone's dialer with the permit's emergency number (911 unless changed with Change), pauses the air and comm reminders, and opens the emergency panel: Read this to the dispatcher (address first), headcount, Text 911 (one text with the needed info, your location and a responder link page), Text Contacts, Copy (responder link), Emergency number called, and Send report to (email) › Send Report Email for whoever the dispatcher directs. Confirm the call on your phone; opening the dialer doesn't prove it connected. When it's over: Note (optional) and Activated by Mistake or Incident Resolved (reminders restart). Ending the incident is NOT permission to re-enter. Today the button doesn't push to the foreman or office; the company's Live now board shows EMERGENCY reported when the phone has signal. Ask also answers "someone is down" questions with an EMERGENCY button and never uses AI for them.
app.title: EMERGENCY button on a permit

app.text: Where: Active Permit › closeout section. Pick Reason for closeout (Completed Normally, Evacuated / Prohibited Condition, Aborted Before Entry, Other), add What happened (optional), tap Close Out Permit. It checks who is still inside and saves the record first. Then optionally Send report to (email) › Send Report Email, and tap Finish & Return Home. The closed permit is in Records with its PDF, backed up to your account (kept forever), and shows in Crew permit records for your foreman and Company permit records for the office. Your foreman gets a push (Crew permit closed). Closing out is not the emergency control.
app.title: Close out a permit

app.text: Where: More › Confined Space Permits › Ventilation Calculator, or Calculators › Confined Space Ventilation. Pick the shape (Rectangular, Cylindrical, I Know the Volume), type the size, pick Air changes per hour (from the job's ventilation plan, or 20 / 40 / 60 ACH). It shows the CFM to blow into the space. There is no officially accepted OSHA ACH rate, and a gas monitor is still required.
app.title: Ventilation calculator from the permit

app.text: Closed permits can't be changed or removed; every version is kept, forever. Where: your own in Records (Permits chip); a foreman's crew in My production › My crew's confined space permits › Crew Permit Records; the office in Records › Company permit records (Load Older Permits, Refresh). Unfinished permit banners in Records open a permit that wasn't closed. Restore Permits From Your Account (Records › On this phone) brings closed permits back to a new phone; photos stay on the phone that took them.
app.title: Permit records: crew and company

app.text: Who: foremen and the office. Where: foreman: Home › My production › your job card › Locates (or Open Locates on a Needs Attention card); office: the job page › Overview › Locates row. Tap Add Dig Ticket, type the 811 ticket number; Called in (today) and Expires fill themselves; tap Save Ticket. Each ticket shows Can dig from and Start work by, counted with the 811 rules of the job's state. The state comes from Change State on the Locates screen, else the job address, else Settings › Company › 811 rules state. Rules for the state (on the Locates screen) shows that state's wait, ticket life, tolerance zone, white lining and sources. Where a state's ticket life is not confirmed the app fills no expiry and Save asks for the date on the ticket. The numbers differ by state (for example a 28-day ticket in California and 14 working days in Texas), so go by the job's state, not by habit. Several tickets per job: Edit, Mark Closed, Reopen. Saves are kept on the phone and sent with signal; a refused one offers Fix and Send Again or Discard. Pipelayers don't keep tickets.
app.title: Add an 811 dig ticket (locates)

app.text: An open ticket on your jobs alerts 7 days before it expires, 2 days before, and on the day: a push (Locate tickets expiring) to the job's foremen and PMs/supers, a morning email line for the PM, and a foreman Needs Attention card (amber within 7 days, red within 2 or expired: "don't dig until it's refreshed. Call 811 for a new ticket"). The card can be snoozed only until the deadline day; then only Minimize for today.
app.title: Locate ticket alerts

app.text: Where: Company Home › Company inspections & tests › Add Inspection or Test (or the job's Inspections & daily reports). Fill Job number, Type (Inspection, Pressure test, Mandrel test, CCTV inspection, Compaction test, Other), Details, Station (or start of range) / To station or Place, Scheduled date (optional), Assigned foreman, Note for the foreman, and tap Add Item. Edit, Cancel Item (with a reason) and Amend keep a history. Each job shows open, done and failed counts.
app.title: Set up inspections and tests on a job (office)

app.text: Where: Home › My inspections & tests (or the Needs Attention card "N inspections and tests due" › Open My Inspections). Tap Check Off on the item, pick Pass, Fail or Partial, type the Inspector's name, Agency or company, Date, Time and Time zone, Notes (optional), Add Photo, and tap Save Check-Off. A check-off can't be changed later. A Fail stays open for the retest unless you tick "Close this item with no retest". A failed item offers Add Rework (a job book rework entry). Done items show on the daily report's Inspections & Tests. Only the assigned foreman checks off; super/PM check-off needs a server update.
app.title: Check off an inspection or test (foreman)

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Company › Company equipment › Edit (company account, PMs, supers). Add a piece: Name, Unit no., Cost code, then Add. Each piece has Edit and Retire; retired pieces have Return. Every crew member can pick from the active list on the daily report and production forms. Kept on the phone for no-signal days; changes need signal. Company vehicles can go on the list too.
app.title: Company equipment list (office)

app.text: Where: the job page › Equipment tab › Add Equipment. Pick from Company equipment or type a name (tick Rental for a rental), Unit no., Cost code. Edit or Remove a piece. The tab totals hours used, idle and down for each piece (today, last 7 days, % of budget hours) from run and daily reports, counted once. Saved with the job plan (signal needed).
app.title: Equipment on a job (Equipment tab)

app.text: Equipment hours come in three ways: the Crew & Equipment Log on a run (check machines in and out), the production form's Equipment hours (Used h, Idle h, Down h per piece; + Add equipment…), and the daily report's Equipment on Site (filled from the runs; change the hours if needed). A breakdown in Run Notes (Breakdown? Yes, it broke down + Downtime) or Down hours on My crew production offers Add a Delay so the lost time reaches the daily report.
app.title: Enter equipment hours, idle and down time

app.text: Coming with equipment maintenance: manufacturer service schedules filled in from make and model (engine hours or miles), a warning when a piece assigned to a job may come due during it, a push to the last foreman when no hours were entered in two weeks, and alerts to supers/PMs for overdue or upcoming service (default 7 days or 40 hours ahead). The intervals are in the data library under Equipment service intervals. Always check the operator's manual.
app.title: Equipment maintenance reminders (coming)

app.text: Where: Company Home › Jobs › New job. Step 1 Details: Job number (required; a number already in use opens that job), Job name, City, State (sets the job's weather; prefilled from your last job), Start date (optional), then Create Job. Step 2 the plan (categories and planned amounts). Step 3 extras: materials, trench settings, PMs & supers, or Skip for now. Needs signal.
app.title: Create a new job (office)

app.text: Where: Company Home › tap a job. Top: % complete bar, hours-budget pace, materials (used / ordered / expected), alerts. Tabs: Overview (live now, crew today, schedule, waiting on foremen, run reports, job book, locates, inspections, recent documents, PMs & supers), Waiting, Materials, Equipment, Production. Edit project opens: Job plan, Materials, Trench settings, PMs & supers, Job details (name, address, start date), Schedule. Refresh reloads.
app.title: The job page (office)

app.text: Where: job page › Edit project › Job plan (or Production tab › Edit Plan). For each category: Category name, Unit, Planned, Budget hours (whole category) or Budget hours per unit, Alert at (% of planned) (Add an Alert for more), Cost code. Add Category for more; default categories are Demo, Excavation, Pipe Installed, Backfill, Restoration, Structures (names and count editable). Equipment rows: Equipment, Unit #, Cost code (Add Equipment). Tap Save Plan. Every other PM/super on the job (and the company account if owner copies is on) gets a push (Plan changes) and a Home alert. Foremen can't edit plans. A category with no Planned shows the amount done (e.g. 400 LF) instead of a %.
app.title: Edit the job plan (categories, planned amounts, budget hours)

app.text: Where: job page › Materials tab › Add Material. Type (Pipe, Bedding / Shading, Road base, Asphalt, Concrete, Fittings, Structures, Other), Material, how used is counted (pipe from footage, bedding/shading calculated from footage × trench width × thickness plus allowance, or by hand), Cost code, Expected, Alert %, Lead time. Each material shows Used / Ordered / Expected with Details, Add Order (amount, expected delivery date), Record Use, Add to Expected, Edit. Delivery tickets count automatically. A material alert (push Material alerts) goes to the job's PMs/supers when use reaches the alert % of what's ordered, or when it's time to order (lead time: "Order by Nov 3"). No prices anywhere.
app.title: Materials: add, order, record use (office)

app.text: Where: Home › New › Work without a run (foremen, PMs, supers). Pick the job and work date, stations from-to and/or footage installed, the pipe / bedding / shading from the job's list, thicknesses and trench width (blank = the job's), the plan's other quantities, crew hours and equipment hours, a note and photos, then Save Entry (Clear Form starts over). It becomes one normal production entry, counts like a run and shows on My production, the job page and the daily report. The company account uses the job page › Production › Add work done by hand instead.
app.title: Work without a run (production with no grade)

app.text: Where: job page › Overview › Schedule › Set End Date (or Edit project › Schedule). Set the end date, milestones, checkpoints and holidays. The app projects the finish from the last 7 days' pace per item (work days Mon–Fri minus holidays). A push (Schedule) goes when a job falls behind its end date or hits a checkpoint.
app.title: Job schedule and end date

app.text: Where: job page › Edit project › PMs & supers. Pick who is on the job. They get its alerts (push right away, one morning email on days something needs a look) and plan-change alerts. A job with none sends alerts to every PM and super in the company, and to the owner only when there are none.
app.title: Assign PMs and supers to a job

app.text: Where: foreman: Home › New › Job book entry (opens on the Current job); office: job page › Overview › Job book row. Raise an Issue (mark it blocking if it stops work; Close Issue later), Add Rework (hours, from a failed inspection too), Add Safety Event (Near miss, First aid, Incident, Property damage, Stop work; no medical details). Photos allowed. Saved on the phone first and sent with signal. Safety events push to the office (Safety events). The closeout checklist (Punch list clear, Restoration complete, As-builts sent, Final inspections done, Materials returned, Tickets reconciled, Owner sign-off) shows at 100% or past the end date.
app.title: Job book: issues, rework, safety events, closeout

app.text: Where: Company Home › Company production. Live now: active runs and permits as crews' phones last sent them (not live if a phone is offline; nobody is alerted from it; Refresh Live Now). Then every job: % complete per category, today's work, pace vs budget hours, runs waiting for a foreman, edits waiting, materials, and Crew pairings. It is the company's stats page, closed jobs included. Production counts only what is synced and approved by the counting rules.
app.title: Company production and Live now (office)

app.text: Where: Home › My production (it moved from Records to Home). Shows Today and Earlier entries, sync status (Sync Now, Try Again, Send Earlier Production), My crew now and crew links (foremen), My foreman (pipelayers), Runs waiting for a foreman, changes waiting for approval, Your jobs (company progress per category and your work today, with Locates for foremen), and Field tickets. Enter each day's own work, not a running total. The Home tab shows a badge when runs wait for you. The company account has no My production.
app.title: My production screen

app.text: Home › Needs Attention lists what needs you: inspections due, locates expiring, runs waiting, crew still checked in, no cloud copy, reports not sent, unsigned dailies, time zone not set, nudges, sent-back reports and more. Each card has a button that opens the right screen (Open Locates, Open My Production, Open My Inspections, Open Run, Open Records, Choose Time Zone …). Permit, emergency and not-saved cards always stay.
app.title: Needs Attention cards on Home

app.text: Where: the ⋯ on a Home › Needs Attention card (or the same ⋯ on the row at the top of the screen the card opened). Remind Me Later: In 1 hour, Tomorrow morning (6 AM), In 3 days, or Minimize (until the problem changes). Deadline cards (like locates) can be put off only until the deadline day, then only Minimize for today. Permit, confined space, emergency, air test and not-saved cards can't be snoozed. Snoozed cards move to Snoozed (N) as one-line rows ("Back tomorrow 6:00 AM"); tap one to bring it back. A new problem on the same card shows again. Your choice follows your account to other phones.
app.title: Snooze or minimize an alert (Remind me later)

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Push notifications › Turn On Notifications, then allow it on the phone. Send a Test Notification checks it. Turn Off on This Phone stops them on this phone. On an iPhone, add the app to your Home Screen first (Share › Add to Home Screen), open it there, log in and turn notifications on there. Notifications are short and general ("2 runs waiting"); they never include report contents, names or readings. Not for emergencies: confined space emergencies keep the alarm on the phone and the email.
app.title: Turn on push notifications

app.text: Settings › Push notifications lists only the ones your role gets: Runs waiting for me (foremen: pipelayers' runs assigned or held for you), Management reports arrived (company account), Run still open reminder (a run you started hours ago never ended), Material alerts (office), Nudges (crew members), Crew permit closed (foremen), Permit checks due (your open permit's air test / comm check), Locate tickets expiring (foremen and office), Weather alerts (Sunday 4 PM) and Evening before (6 PM), Safety events (office), Schedule (office), Plan changes (PMs/supers on the job), Run reports sent back (your run sent back), Delays & extra work (company account and PMs), Crew production reminders (foremen). Each has its own switch.
app.title: Which push notifications exist and who gets them

app.text: Where: Account & Settings › Push notifications › Weather alerts / Evening before, and Week Ahead. Sunday 4 PM: bad weather on your jobs this week; Evening before: 6 PM before a work day with bad weather. Week Ahead shows the forecast for your jobs (needs signal and the job's City, State).
app.title: Weather alerts and Week ahead

app.text: Where: Records tab. One list, newest first, of every report your account can open: runs, permits, dailies, tickets, management reports, from the company server merged with this phone's own. Chips: All, Runs, Permits, Dailies (foremen and up), Tickets, Mgmt reports, Inbox. Filters: Date, Job, People (the people below you), and On this phone. Tap a row to open it (most open in the PDF viewer). Refresh and Load more at the bottom. A banner shows when something waits (N not sent yet, Unfinished permit). Works offline with this phone's records.
app.title: Records tab: find any report

app.text: Where: Records › the On this phone chip in the filter row (tap its × to turn it off). It shows the records kept on this phone with every action: Search, Time period, Status, Report type, Jobsite filters; each record has View, Email a Copy and More actions (Download PDF, Mark Sent / Mark Emailed, Retry Sync, Adjust End Time, Resume This Run, Emergency Report PDF, Export Record Data (JSON), Delete). Download all: Spreadsheet, PDF or Both. Permit backup: Restore Permits From Your Account. Photos, Stats and Quick Run are kept only on this phone; download a copy to keep them.
app.title: On this phone filter (every action on your phone's records)

app.text: Email a Copy (Records › On this phone › the record) opens your phone's email app with the report as text; nothing is sent until you send it there. To attach the PDF, Download PDF first (or Share from the PDF viewer). Email Reports Not Emailed Yet sends the rest in one go (individual users; company crews send in the app instead). Download all: Spreadsheet, PDF or Both. Stats: Save / Share Stats, Download Spreadsheet, Download PDF. Job Summary: Download Job Summary PDF. Daily report: PDF after signing. Permits: Send Report Email at closeout or in an emergency.
app.title: Email or export reports

app.text: Every View opens the in-app PDF viewer: the same PDF the Download button makes. Buttons: zoom (100%, 150%, 200%), Download, Share (phones that can), Text version. Back closes it. Reports carry every time stamp, the company logo and "Made with The Pipelayer's Bible"; photos show as Photo 1, Photo 2 … with a photo section.
app.title: PDF viewer

app.text: Where: Records › On this phone › the run › More actions › Delete. It asks first, then whether to also remove it from Stats. A foreman can delete his crew's runs; the office can too. When production was entered for it, the app asks whether to take it off the company totals (keep it if the work was real); the company keeps the history.
app.title: Delete a run

app.text: Where: Records › the "N not sent yet" banner. Jobs Not Sent lists jobs on this phone with records not sent yet (Show All Jobs for all). Add Job adds a job number or jobsite to this phone's list only; it isn't sent anywhere or filled into a run.
app.title: Jobs Not Sent list

app.text: The app works with no signal: runs, permits, calculators, tickets, notes, production and dailies are saved on this phone first and sent by themselves when there's signal. Chips say where things are: Saved on this phone, Not synced yet, Sending when there's signal, Synced. "NOT saved on this phone" (red) means keep the app open and tap Retry Save. Admin changes (crew members, job plans, materials, logo, new job, equipment list) need signal and aren't queued. AI needs signal. Lists from the company server show the last copy with its time ("From this phone, as of …").
app.title: Working offline and how syncing works

app.text: When a run's cloud backup failed, Records (All) shows the run with "No cloud copy" and a Retry Sync button; Records › On this phone has it too, and a Needs Attention card says "Saved on this phone. Tap Retry Sync in Records." Tap Retry Sync with signal while signed in. If you're signed out it says "Not synced: not signed in. Log in with signal, then tap Retry Sync."
app.title: Retry Sync (a run with no cloud copy)

app.text: A red banner means something isn't saved on this phone yet: Run Results "NOT saved to Records yet … Tap Retry Save", note photos "Tap Retry Photos before closing the app", a permit's Retry Save / Retry Now. Tap the button and keep the app open until it says saved. These cards can't be snoozed. My production: Sync Now sends waiting production; Try Again reloads.
app.title: Retry Save, Retry Photos and other not-saved banners

app.text: Where: Home › New › Management report. Pick Category (Safety, Equipment, HR / Personnel, General / Other), write What's going on? (up to 3,000 characters), + Add Photo, choose Send this With My Name or Anonymous, and tap Send Report. It goes to your company's owner and managers in the app (no email). Anonymous reports can never be traced to you, not even by the app owner. No one to send to yet? Save Without Sending keeps it marked Not sent. You get a Report Receipt (View Report). Not an emergency line: for anything urgent, call. Company accounts and PMs receive reports instead.
app.title: Send a management report (safety, equipment, HR)

app.text: Where: Records › My Management Reports (or the Mgmt reports chip). Lists saved, waiting and sent reports with replies; tap Check for Replies. Anonymous senders see replies on their own phone too.
app.title: Replies to your management reports

app.text: Where: Company Home › Management inbox tile (Records › Inbox). Tap a report to read it; anonymous ones show no name, no account, only the hour sent. Type a reply and tap Send Reply (the sender reads it on their phone). Refresh reloads. Push: Management reports arrived.
app.title: Management inbox (office)

app.text: Where: More › Toolbox Talks. Search talks or pick a category. Foremen also get a schedule (weekdays, every week or every 2 weeks, default Monday), a queue (Add Talks, reorder, remove), Pick one at random (skips talks given recently), and Mark as Given: Date, Job (your Current job), Crew there (Add a name), then Save. On a due day Home shows "Toolbox talk today: <title>" until one is given. The office reads talks given per job, and the daily report lists the day's talks.
app.title: Toolbox Talks

app.text: Where: More › Education & Reference. Search ("What are you trying to understand?"), Browse all topics (Rod Units & Grade Math, Reading Stationing & Cutsheets, Pipe Cross-Section, Slope & Grade, Bends & Fittings, Flow & Volume, Trenching & Excavation, Pipe & Materials, Confined Space, Concrete & Slurry, Safety Facts, Glossary), lessons, and Saved (tap ☆ Save on any page). Works offline. Can't find it? Ask a question (AI) opens Ask.
app.title: Education & Reference

app.text: Where: More › Stats. Counts runs locked with a pipe type, kept on this phone only. Filters: Time period, Pipe type, Jobsite. Share and download: Save / Share Stats (opens your email app with a text summary), Download Spreadsheet, Download PDF, Download Both. Manage Stats: Clear All Stats Data (this phone only; download first). Stats and Job Summary count differently, so totals can differ.
app.title: Stats

app.text: Where: More › Job Summary. Pick a Job Number. It rolls up every locked run on this phone under that job: footage, pipe takeoff by size, volumes, crew, confined space entries. Download Job Summary PDF. It reads this phone's Records only; other phones' runs and company records aren't in it.
app.title: Job Summary

app.text: Calculators tab, by group. Grade & Elevation: Rod Reading → Elevation, Slope / Grade Converter, Tenths ↔ Inches, Construction Calculator, Backfill Lift Count, Structure Bedding. Trench & Backfill: Trench Sloping, Confined Space Ventilation. Pipe & Flow: Pipe Weight, Manning's Equation, Flush / Flow Rate, Material Volume, Bedding & Shading, Bend Offset. Structures: Manhole Rim-to-Invert Depth. Also Quick Run (Home). Every calculator answers as you type; there is no Calculate button. Each has Add to Home. Formulas and inputs are in the data library.
app.title: Calculators list

app.text: Type the inputs and the answer shows at once (no Calculate button). A wrong entry gets one quiet line when you leave the field. Change an input and the answer updates; an out-of-date answer can't be copied or added to a note. Copy calculation copies the answer text. Entries are kept when you leave a calculator (answers redo themselves when you come back). Smart defaults: Manning's diameter and n, Pipe Weight material, OD and wall, Bedding trench width and thickness, and rod type come from your last run (marked auto; typing makes it yours).
app.title: Using a calculator: live answers, copy, add to note

app.text: Where: Run Results › a grade row's ⋯ menu. Bend Offset, Structure Bedding (invert, wall and BOP from that row), Trench Sloping (depth and trench width from the run) and Rod Reading → Elevation (HI from the run; Lenker runs don't need it). Back returns to the row.
app.title: Calculators from a grade row

app.text: Where: Calculators › Rod Reading → Elevation. Pick Engineer's Rod or Architect's Rod (a Lenker rod reads elevation directly). Enter Known elevation (ft) and Rod reading at known point to get the HI, then each Rod reading at new point gives its elevation. Label (optional) › + Add to List keeps a list of shots (Clear, Undo); the list isn't saved and clears when the app closes.
app.title: Rod Reading → Elevation: shoot several points

app.text: Where: Calculators › Construction Calculator. Keypad with C, CE, ⌫, Feet, Inch, /, ÷, ×, −, +, ±, =, unit keys ft-in, ft, in, m, mm, and fraction setting 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16. Math is exact fractions, rounded only for display. A typed fraction (3/8) is inches; a plain number takes the last unit used. The Tape keeps every step (Copy, Clear) until the app closes.
app.title: Construction Calculator (feet-inch-fraction)

app.text: Where: the Ask tab (or Education & Reference › Can't find it? Ask a question (AI)). It opens over the screen you're on, so nothing is lost; the screen sets "Asking about" (tap to ask about any topic instead). Type Your question and tap Ask. Answers come from the app's Education pages with links to them ("From this app:"), marked "AI answer · can be wrong". Clear These Answers empties the list. Needs signal and a paid plan, with a daily limit ("You've used today's N AI requests. It resets tomorrow."). Questions are sent to Anthropic to be read and not stored by the app; don't use AI with confidential project info.
app.title: Ask: questions about the app or the trade

app.text: Ask never decides whether a space or trench is safe to enter, whether a permit can be signed, or whether readings are OK to go in: it answers "Stop and ask your entry supervisor / competent person" with the rule pages, and nothing is sent to AI. If a question sounds like an emergency now (someone down, not responding, cave-in, gas alarm going off) it answers at once: get out, don't go in after them unless trained and equipped, call, with an EMERGENCY button. Follow your competent person and your site's safety program.
app.title: What Ask won't answer

app.text: Run Setup › Pipe type fills Wall thickness (ft) and the pipe laying length from the app's pipe table (PB_PIPE_INDEX), marked auto. Wall = (OD − ID) / 2, measured invert to outside bottom, so BOP = INV − wall; ductile iron's includes the cement lining. The table is in inches; the run form uses feet (inches ÷ 12, 3 decimals). Variants used: C900 DR18, ductile iron lowest standard class + lining, solid-wall HDPE DR17, concrete wall B. Laying length is the common stick length (SDR 35 14 ft, C900 and DI 20 ft, concrete 8 ft, corrugated HDPE 20 ft); none for solid-wall HDPE (butt-fused), clay, steel, Sch 40/80. A typed value always wins; a pipe type change refills only app-filled boxes. Blank Pipe type = "PVC SDR 35 (auto)". Source: /home/claude/feat_fitdata/pipe_index.json.
app.title: How the app fills wall thickness and laying length (PB_PIPE_INDEX)

app.text: A fitting's laying length is the length along the main line it takes up, from where the incoming pipe end stops to where the outgoing pipe end starts, both fully inserted (socket bottom to socket bottom; a bend is inlet center-to-socket-bottom plus outlet center-to-socket-bottom; butt-fused and welded fittings are the whole fitting). The table (PB_FIT_LAY_INDEX) is in INCHES by pipe type, fitting (90°, 45°, 22.5°, 11.25° bends, tee, wye, tee-wye, coupling, reducer) and nominal size; branch fittings and reducers are "main x branch" / "large x small". On Run Setup a Fitting hub fills Laying length (ft) = inches ÷ 12, marked auto. The hub station is the fitting's center: pipe in stops at station − L/2, pipe out starts at station + L/2; grades don't change. In large pipe it can be several feet. Source: /home/claude/feat_fitdata/fitlen_index.json (REPORT.md).

app.text: Coming with equipment maintenance: the app will fill a machine's service schedule from its make and model (from /home/claude/feat_equipmaint/maint_index.json, built Nov 3 2026, research only). Lookup order: the model's own list (a model may point to another model's list), else the make's default, else a generic fallback by kind (machines in engine hours; gas pickups, diesel pickups and heavy trucks in miles), always plus the universal daily (10-hour) checks. Higher-hour services include the lower-hour items due at the same time. "Severe" = construction/vocational use; use those steps for work trucks. Confidence: high = read from the OEM document; medium = OEM marketing/press, a CMMS page built from the manual, a dealer, or a sibling model; low = derived or unclear. Every schedule must show "check your operator's manual". Not found (generic fallback used): Hitachi ZX, Takeuchi, Case 580/590 and skid steers, Komatsu dozers/loaders, Volvo filters, Cat 9xx loaders, Cat D3–D5, Ram 1500 and gas HD, Ford/GM gas HD, International A26, Ditch Witch, vac trucks, most rollers.

app.text: Inputs: rod type (Engineer's Rod in decimal feet, or Architect's Rod in feet-inches-sixteenths), Known elevation (ft), Rod reading at known point, Rod reading at new point. Formula: HI (height of instrument) = known elevation + rod reading at the known point; new elevation = HI − rod reading at the new point. Readings can't be negative (a rod is read up from its foot). A Lenker rod reads elevation directly, so it isn't needed. From a grade row the known elevation is that row's invert and the reading is HI − invert. Shots can be listed with a label (+ Add to List); the list isn't saved.
app.title: Rod Reading → Elevation formula

app.text: Inputs: rod (Lenker, Engineer's, Architect's), Reading at Start, Reading at End, Slope (%), Distance (ft), Row spacing (ft, blank = 10). Enter any three; the fourth is solved. Quick Run is fall-positive (+ = drops start to end). Lenker (readings are elevations): end = start − slope% / 100 × distance; slope% = (start − end) / distance × 100. Engineer's / Architect's (rod readings grow as the grade drops): end reading = start reading + slope% / 100 × distance; slope% = (end − start) / distance × 100. Distance must be more than 0. Full runs and Records use rise-positive grade: grade % = (end invert − start invert) ÷ distance × 100.
app.title: Quick Run formula (grade, readings, distance)

app.text: Pick Percent, Ratio (1:X) or Degrees and type one value (greater than 0). Percent → ratio X = 100 ÷ %; degrees = atan(% ÷ 100). Ratio 1:X → % = 100 ÷ X; degrees = atan(1 ÷ X). Degrees (below 90) → % = tan(deg) × 100; X = 1 ÷ tan(deg). The ratio is written rise : run (2% = 1 : 50); OSHA's trench tables write run : rise.
app.title: Slope / Grade Converter formula

app.text: Decimal feet → feet-inches: feet = whole part; inches = remainder × 12; fraction = leftover inches rounded to the nearest 1/16". Example 0.35 ft = 0' 4-3/16". Feet - Inches - Fraction → decimal feet = feet + inches ÷ 12 + fraction ÷ 12, shown to 3 places. Both directions answer as you type.
app.title: Tenths ↔ Inches formula

app.text: Keypad math in exact fractions: lengths in inches, areas in square inches, volumes in cubic inches, rounded only for display to the chosen 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 or 1/16. Chain math left to right like a tape calculator. A typed fraction (3/8) is inches; a plain number beside a length takes the last unit key used on it (12' + 3 = 15'; 6" + 3 = 9"); beside an area it is square feet, a volume cubic feet. A plain number given to a unit key (ft-in, ft, in, m, mm) is decimal feet (0.35 then ft-in = 4-3/16"). Length × length = area, × again = volume. The fraction setting is saved; the tape lasts until the app closes.
app.title: Construction Calculator (feet-inch-fraction math)

app.text: Inputs: Offset (ft, more than 0), Bend angle (each fitting): 11.25°, 22.5° or 45°, Fitting 1 and Fitting 2 C-E (center-to-end, ft, optional: fitting center to the stop shoulder inside the bell). Multiplier = 1 ÷ sin(angle): 11.25° = 5.126, 22.5° = 2.613, 45° = 1.414. Vertex-to-vertex distance (travel) = offset × multiplier. With C-E: pipe cut length (stop to stop) = travel − C-E1 − C-E2 (zero or less = the fittings don't fit that offset). Example: 2 ft offset with 45s = 2.828 ft vertex to vertex.
app.title: Bend Offset formula

app.text: Pick the reference: Invert (Invert elevation, optional Wall thickness shows BOP = invert − wall) or BOP (BOP elevation). Inputs: Distance, invert (or BOP) to bottom of manhole (ft), Required bedding thickness (ft), optional Pad length and Pad width (ft), Quantity (structures this size). Top of bedding = reference − distance; bottom of bedding = top − thickness. Bedding volume (estimate) = pad length × pad width × thickness ÷ 27 × quantity, in yd³, with weight in tons (see material densities). From a grade row the invert, wall and BOP come from that row.
app.title: Structure Bedding formula

app.text: Inputs: Total depth to backfill (ft, compacted/final), Max loose lift thickness (in, before compaction), Loose-to-compacted shrink (Gravel / rock 25%, Sand 30%, Silt / loam 30%, Clay 35%, or Other). Compacted lift = loose lift × (1 − shrink). Number of lifts = round up (depth in inches ÷ compacted lift). Loose thickness per lift (evened out) = (depth in inches ÷ lifts) ÷ (1 − shrink), compacting to depth ÷ lifts. The shrink presets are a rough rule of thumb (loose fill usually loses 25–35%; source unknown per the owner): use your compaction spec or the engineer's numbers.
app.title: Backfill Lift Count formula
app.table_source: app code pbCalcLifts; shrink presets: rule of thumb, source unknown

app.text: Inputs: Trench depth (ft), Soil type, optional Trench bottom width (ft), and for Type A the unsupported vertical lower portion option. Maximum allowable slopes (run:rise, from OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P Appendix B Table B-1): Stable Rock vertical (90°); Type A 0.75:1 (53°); Type A short-term (12 ft or less, open 24 hours or less) 0.5:1 (63°); Type B 1:1 (45°); Type C 1.5:1 (34°). Horizontal offset each side = depth × ratio; required top width = bottom width + 2 × offset (no bottom width: the drawing uses 2 ft as an example). Type A vertical lower portion (12 ft or less, no shoring): up to 3.5 ft vertical at the bottom, then 0.75:1 above it at 8 ft or less, 1:1 deeper; offset = (depth − vertical part) × ratio. At 20 ft or deeper (exactly 20 ft included) no slope is given and the result says "Engineer Required": Table B-1 covers excavations "less than 20 feet deep", and note 3 says: "Sloping or benching for excavations greater than 20 feet deep shall be designed by a registered professional engineer" (Table B-1 note 3).
app.title: Trench Sloping formula (OSHA Appendix B)
app.table_source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P App. B Table B-1; app code TRENCH_SLOPES / pbCalcTrench

app.text: Inputs: shape Rectangular (Length, Width, Depth ft), Cylindrical (Diameter ft, Depth ft) or I Know the Volume (ft³), and Air changes per hour: from the job's ventilation plan, or presets 20, 40, 60 ACH. Volume: rectangle L × W × D; cylinder π × (dia ÷ 2)² × depth. Airflow needed (CFM) = volume × ACH ÷ 60. A blower's rated CFM drops with hose length and bends. There is no officially accepted (OSHA) air-changes-per-hour rate; the presets come from manufacturer guidance (Allegro Industries), a university procedure (MIT) and research hosted by CDC/NIOSH. A gas monitor is still required.
app.title: Confined Space Ventilation formula
app.table_source: app code pbCalcVent; ACH presets: Allegro Industries, MIT procedure, CDC/NIOSH

app.text: Inputs: Outside diameter (in), Wall thickness (in), Length (ft), Material density. ID = OD − 2 × wall. Cross-section area (ft²) = π ÷ 4 × ((OD ÷ 12)² − (ID ÷ 12)²). Weight = area × length × density; weight per foot = weight ÷ length. Densities (lb/ft³): Ductile Iron ~450, PVC (Sch 40, Sch 80, C900, SDR 35) ~90, Solid-Wall HDPE ~59, Corrugated HDPE 59 treated as a solid wall (overstates the real weight; use the maker's number), Steel ~490, Concrete ~150, or Other. Plain wall only: bells and lining not counted; for a lift plan use the manufacturer's weight. OD and wall fill from the run's pipe (auto): wall in = run wall ft × 12, OD = pipe ID + 2 × wall.
app.title: Pipe Weight formula
app.table_source: app code pbCalcPipeWeight (densities in the Material list)

app.text: Inputs: Pipe diameter (in), Slope (%), Manning's n: PVC / HDPE 0.010, Concrete / Vitrified Clay / Lined Ductile Iron 0.013, Corrugated Metal 0.024, or Other. Full pipe: area A = π ÷ 4 × D² (D in ft), hydraulic radius R = D ÷ 4, S = slope ÷ 100. Velocity V (ft/s) = 1.49 ÷ n × R^(2/3) × √S. Capacity Q (ft³/s) = V × A; GPM = Q × 448.831. Below 2 ft/s is flagged as under the common self-cleansing benchmark (solids may settle).
app.title: Manning's Equation formula (full pipe)

app.text: Inputs: Pitot (velocity) pressure at the outlet (psi), Discharge opening diameter (in; the opening, not the pipe), Discharge coefficient C: Smooth and rounded outlet 0.90, Square and sharp-edged outlet 0.80, Square, projecting into barrel 0.70, With a stream straightener 0.95 (device value; verify with its maker), or Other; optional Target gallons. Flow (GPM) = 29.83 × C × d² × √P. Time to reach the target = gallons ÷ GPM, shown in minutes and seconds. The C values are standard NFPA/IFSTA coefficients.
app.title: Flush / Flow Rate formula
app.table_source: app code pbCalcFlow; C values NFPA/IFSTA

app.text: Shapes (feet unless marked): Rectangular L × W × D. Trapezoid ((top width + bottom width) ÷ 2) × depth × length. Triangular ½ × base × height × depth. Cylindrical π × (dia in ÷ 12 ÷ 2)² × length. Pie Slice, True Circle: (angle ÷ 360) × π × r² × depth, arc length (angle ÷ 360) × 2πr. Pie Slice, Custom Curve (hand-shaped curve): area = ½ × L² × sin(angle) + ⅔ × chord × sagitta, where chord = 2L × sin(angle ÷ 2) and sagitta = corner-to-farthest-point − L × cos(angle ÷ 2); times depth. Encasement: L × W × D minus each pipe's π × (OD in ÷ 24)² × length × count (+ Add Another Pipe Size). Times Quantity. Shown in Cubic Yards (ft³ ÷ 27), Cubic Feet or Gallons (ft³ × 7.48052), with weight in tons for a picked material (see material densities).
app.title: Material Volume formulas

app.text: Pick Bedding, Shading or both; one or more sections (Add Section for another size): Length (ft), Trench width (ft), Bedding thickness (ft); for shading the Pipe (presets: 4" SDR 35 4.215" OD, 6" 6.275", 8" 8.400", 10" 10.500", 12" 12.500", 15" 15.300"; 4" DIP / C900 4.80", 6" 6.90", 8" 9.05", 10" 11.10", 12" 13.20", or type the OD) and Shading over the top of the pipe (ft). Bedding ft³ = L × W × T. Shading ft³ = L × (W × (OD ft + shading) − π × OD ft² ÷ 4). Yd³ = ft³ ÷ 27. To order = yd³ × (1 + Compaction allowance), default 15%. Bedding + shading of the same material are also totaled. Weight in tons uses the material densities. Always an estimate.
app.title: Bedding & Shading formula

app.text: Inputs: Rim elevation (ft), Invert elevation (ft), optional Cone/top section height (ft) and Barrel section height (ft). Total structure depth = rim − invert (rim must be higher). Full barrel sections = round down ((depth − cone) ÷ barrel height); leftover = depth − cone − sections × barrel. A simplified height budget: verify the assembly against the approved detail.
app.title: Manhole Rim-to-Invert Depth formula
