field.text: Every public works job runs on a stack of documents, and the contract lists them. The usual order when they conflict: change orders and addenda, special provisions (project specs), the plans, the agency's own standard plans and specifications, then the general standard spec book the agency adopts (a state DOT spec like Caltrans, TxDOT or WSDOT, or a regional public works spec like the Greenbook in Southern California, MAG in Phoenix, PAG in Tucson, NCTCOG in Dallas-Fort Worth, APWA KC Metro in Kansas City, ISPWC in Idaho, MPWSS in Montana, Utah MOSS, SUDAS in Iowa, CEAM in Minnesota, the Wisconsin sewer and water specs, the Illinois water and sewer specs, Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications in Las Vegas, RTC Washoe Orange Book in Reno), then referenced standards (AWWA, ASTM, OSHA). Water and sewer design in ten Midwestern and Northeastern states follows the Ten States Standards. Private site work follows the project specs and the city or water district's standards for anything it will own. Always check the edition: agencies adopt specific years.
field.title: Which spec book governs a job, anywhere in the US
field.topic: Construction specs by state and region
field.source: Standard contract document practice; regional public works specification publishers

field.text: Washington (WSDOT Standard Specifications M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-08, general pipe installation). Trench: remove ledge rock, boulders and stones to give at least 6 inches clearance under all parts of the pipe; keep the toe of the spoil pile at least 2 feet from the trench edge; shoring is called for in trenches 4 feet or deeper that don't meet the open-pit rules of 3-07.3(3)B (7-08.3(1)A). Bedding: compact to 90 percent of maximum density, in lifts no more than 6 inches thick along the sides of the pipe; fix line and grade by scraping or filling under the barrel, never by blocking or wedging (7-08.3(1)C). Backfill (7-08.3(3)): pipe zone compacted to 90 percent, no rocks or lumps over 3 inches; under existing pavement or roadways 6-inch layers at 95 percent; in non-traffic areas 6-inch layers at 85 percent. No tractors or heavy equipment over the pipe until backfill is 3 feet above the top of the pipe. Laying tolerance: invert within plus or minus 0.03 foot at the time of backfill, and never a reverse slope (7-08.3(2)B). Your contract's special provisions and the city's own amendments can change these numbers.
field.title: Washington WSDOT pipe trench, bedding, backfill, and cover before equipment runs over new pipe (Section 7-08)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-09, water mains). Minimum cover 36 inches over the top of the pipe; at least 1 foot over valve operating nuts. Trench width up to 1 foot above the pipe: no more than 30 inches or 1.5 times the pipe outside diameter plus 18 inches, whichever is greater. Bedding compacted to 95 percent of maximum density (7-09.3(9)); backfill to at least 95 percent, in layers of 6 inches loose or less under paved areas (7-09.3(11)). Hydrostatic test (7-09.3(23)): 150 psi above operating pressure and never less than 225 psi; sections normally no longer than 1,500 feet; pump up, stop for 15 minutes, pump back to test pressure; allowable leakage L = S x D x square root of P / 266,400 (L gallons per hour, S feet of pipe, D inches, P psi). Disinfection (7-09.3(24)): at least 50 mg/L chlorine to start, hold at least 24 hours, at least 25 mg/L left after 24 hours; flush at 2.5 feet per second or more; dechlorinate the flush water to 0.1 ppm or less and pH 6.5 to 8.5. Services 2 inch and smaller need 3 feet of cover (7-15); hydrants need a 3-foot clear radius and the sidewalk flange 2 inches above finished grade (7-14).
field.title: Washington WSDOT water main: cover, backfill, pressure test, disinfection (Section 7-09)
field.topic: Spec books: water main installation, pressure test and disinfection
field.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-17.3(2), sanitary sewers). Clean and test within 15 working days after backfilling. Exfiltration: no more than 0.28 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet, with 6 feet of head over the crown at the upper end (or over groundwater if higher), test length no more than 700 feet, no more than 16 feet of head at the low invert (7-17.3(2)B). Infiltration: 0.16 gallon per hour per inch per 100 feet when groundwater head is 2 feet or less (7-17.3(2)C). Add 0.2 gallon per hour per foot of head for each manhole in the test section (D). Low-pressure air test for pipe 30 inches and smaller: pump to 4 psig, wait at least 2 minutes, then time the drop from 3.5 to 2.5 psig; the time comes from K = 0.0111 x d squared x L and C = 0.0003918 x d x L (E); pipe that does not pass air needs four times that time (F); over 30 inches test each joint under ASTM C1103. Deflection test for thermoplastic pipe: not less than 30 days after trench backfill and compaction are complete, with a mandrel that has an odd number of legs (9 or more) and is 95 percent of the pipe's base inside diameter (G). The Engineer can require TV inspection (H).
field.title: Washington WSDOT sanitary sewer tests: air, water, mandrel, TV (Section 7-17)
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Oregon Standard Specifications Section 00405: trench at least 24 in wide and only as wide as needed to install the pipe safely; pipe zone runs from the top of the bedding to at least 8 in over the pipe, full trench width. Bedding and pipe zone material placed in compacted layers no thicker than 6 in, at -4 to +2 percent of optimum moisture, hand-compacted under the haunches; bedding is 3/4 in-0 aggregate (required with groundwater) or approved sand; rigid pipe zone uses 1 in-0 or 3/4 in-0 aggregate. Trench backfill classes: A native, B 1 in-0 or 3/4 in-0 crushed rock (default), C clean sand, D pit run up to 3 in, E CLSM. Class B compaction (00405.46): at least 95 percent of AASHTO T 99 maximum density under roadway, shoulders and the 2:1 line from the shoulder, 90 percent elsewhere; no free-falling backfill until 3 ft of cover. CLSM: no compaction, plate it 24 hours. Ponding or jetting: not within the roadbed; elsewhere only with written approval, at least 35 psi, jet pipe to within 1 ft of the bottom at 4 ft or less spacing. Sawcut pavement at least 6 in wider than the trench each side.
field.title: Oregon trench width, bedding and backfill (00405)
field.topic: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction (ODOT/APWA)
field.source: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction 2024, Sections 00405, 00415, 00445, 00470, 00495 (Oregon); check the edition and special provisions

field.text: Oregon Sections 00445.72-.73: test after backfill and compaction and before wearing-course paving. Exfiltration: no more than 0.04 gal/hr per inch of diameter per 100 ft (0.3 in arid zones with approval) at 6 ft of head over the high crown or groundwater, no more than 16 ft at the lower invert, after 4 hours of saturation. Air test (time-pressure drop): raise to 4 psi over groundwater back-pressure (add 0.433 psi per ft of water over the crown), stabilize 2 minutes, time the drop from 3.5 to 2.5 psi; PVC and HDPE accept if time is at least T = 0.085 x D x K / Q with K = 0.000419 x D x L (minimum 1.0) and Q = 0.0015; joint tests on 30 in and up must lose less than 1 psi in 5 seconds. Deflection: mandrel at 95 percent of initial ID with at least 9 vanes, no sooner than 30 days after backfill, or video with laser profiling (00415): over 5 percent needs a stamped remediation plan, over 7.5 percent the pipe is replaced. Post-installation video at least 30 days after backfill, before paving.
field.title: Oregon sewer and storm pipe tests (00415, 00445)
field.topic: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction (ODOT/APWA)
field.source: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction 2024, Sections 00405, 00415, 00445, 00470, 00495 (Oregon); check the edition and special provisions

field.text: Oregon Section 00470.71: sanitary manholes tested after backfill, restoration and paving. Hydrostatic: no more than 0.3 gal/hr per ft of head above the invert. Vacuum (ASTM C1244): pull 10 in Hg and time the drop to 9 in Hg; minimum times grow with depth and diameter, for example a 48 in manhole needs 20 seconds up to 8 ft deep, 30 seconds at 12 ft, 40 at 16 ft, 50 at 20 ft, 59 at 24 ft and 74 at 30 ft (depth from top to lowest invert; interpolate). Trench resurfacing (00495): temporary emulsified asphalt at least 1 in thick, within 1/2 in of the existing surface and joints no more than 1/4 in high, kept up until permanent paving per 00744/00745.
field.title: Oregon manhole vacuum test and trench resurfacing (00470, 00495)
field.topic: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction (ODOT/APWA)
field.source: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction 2024, Sections 00405, 00415, 00445, 00470, 00495 (Oregon); check the edition and special provisions

field.text: Utah APWA Manual of Standard Specifications Section 33 05 20 Backfilling Trenches: pipe zone extends to 1 ft above the top of the pipe; backfill compacted to 95 percent or more of standard or modified Proctor (aggregate base uses modified, ASTM D1557; subgrade standard, ASTM D698), verified by nuclear gauge (ASTM D2922); lifts no more than 8 in before compaction with riding equipment, 6 in with hand-held equipment; maximum particle size 3/4 in against plastic pipe; water settling and jetting are not permitted; compaction lots of 200 linear ft per lift; cement-treated (flowable) fill targets 60 psi at 28 days, 90 psi maximum; warning tape at least 6 in wide, 4 mil, 18 in below finished grade.
field.title: Utah MOSS trench backfill (33 05 20)
field.topic: Utah: APWA Manual of Standard Specifications (MOSS)
field.source: APWA Utah Manual of Standard Specifications 2025 (Utah LTAP), Sections 33 05 20, 33 05 25, 33 08 00, 33 11 00 (Utah); check city supplements

field.text: Utah APWA MOSS Section 33 05 25: aggregate base matches existing or at least 8 in, in lifts no more than 8 in, compacted to 95 percent of modified Proctor; asphalt patch thickness is the existing thickness plus 1 in, minimum 4 in (maximum 6 in residential, 8 in non-residential), placed in lifts of at least 3 in compacted to 94 percent of Rice density plus or minus 2; asphalt placed below 40 F is temporary; finished tolerance 1/4 in in 10 ft; notify the engineer within 24 hours (at least 4 hours) before starting.
field.title: Utah MOSS pavement restoration (33 05 25)
field.topic: Utah: APWA Manual of Standard Specifications (MOSS)
field.source: APWA Utah Manual of Standard Specifications 2025 (Utah LTAP), Sections 33 05 20, 33 05 25, 33 08 00, 33 11 00 (Utah); check city supplements

field.text: Utah APWA MOSS Section 33 08 00 commissioning: notify 48 hours before tests; grade tolerance 1/2 in in 10 ft on grades over 1 percent, 1/4 in in 10 ft at 0.5 to 1 percent, 1/4 in in 100 ft under 0.5 percent; alignment within 1 in; infiltration no more than 200 gal per inch of diameter per mile per day; plastic pipe air test allows a 0.5 psi drop (isolated joint test on pipe over 30 in at 3.5 psi, no more than 1 psi drop in 5 seconds); deflection limits PVC 7.5 percent, HDPE and polypropylene 5 percent, ductile iron 3 percent; mandrel with at least 9 runners; CCTV crawl no faster than 30 ft per minute. Section 33 11 00 water: separation from sewer at least 10 ft horizontal and 18 in vertical; at crossings encase 10 ft each side and no water joint within 36 in; thrust blocks cure at least 5 days before the pressure test; cover no more than 72 in unless authorized.
field.title: Utah MOSS pipe acceptance and water line rules (33 08 00, 33 11 00)
field.topic: Utah: APWA Manual of Standard Specifications (MOSS)
field.source: APWA Utah Manual of Standard Specifications 2025 (Utah LTAP), Sections 33 05 20, 33 05 25, 33 08 00, 33 11 00 (Utah); check city supplements

field.text: Iowa SUDAS Section 3010: Class I crushed stone bedding is required for all gravity mains (and for pressure pipe when specified), placed in lifts no more than 6 in, with extra bedding beside the pipe equal to 1/6 of the OD; remove unsuitable soil at least 6 in below and beside the pipe. Zones: haunch (bedding to springline), primary backfill (springline to top of pipe), secondary (top of pipe to 1 ft over). Compaction: Class III and IVA soils 90 percent standard Proctor in the haunch and 95 percent in the primary, secondary and final backfill within the right-of-way (90 percent outside), at optimum to 4 percent over optimum moisture; granular Class II 65 percent relative density (50 percent outside right-of-way). Lifts: 6 in maximum in the pipe zone, 8 in in final backfill more than 3 ft below pavement, 6 in within 3 ft of pavement. Flooding only if the engineer allows. Testing: starting 2 ft over the pipe, at least every 2 vertical ft at 200 ft spacing and at every street crossing.
field.title: Iowa SUDAS trench bedding and backfill (Section 3010)
field.topic: Iowa: SUDAS Statewide Urban Design and Specifications
field.source: SUDAS Standard Specifications Section 3010 Trench Excavation and Backfill (Iowa); check the edition and city supplemental specifications

field.text: Arizona MAG Uniform Standard Specifications (Phoenix area, updated yearly; cities add supplements): Section 601 trench excavation, backfilling and compaction (bedding per 601.4; many utilities require mechanical compaction only and allow water settling only with approval); 610 water line construction (610.6 polyethylene wrap); 611 disinfection; 615 sanitary sewer line construction (615.6 and 615.8 taps and connections, 615.9 cleanouts); 616 reclaimed water; 618 storm drain; 630 valves; 750 ductile iron (750.4 push-on joints); 336 pavement matching and surfacing replacement. Standard Details: 301, 380 and 381 thrust blocks; 303-1 and 303-2 joint restraint; 360 hydrants; 391-1 valve boxes; 404 water and sewer separation; 424 air release manholes; 426 drop manholes; 440-1 sewer taps; 441 cleanouts. Utilities often add rules, for example aggregate base 4 in under and 12 in over water and sewer lines, a 200 ppm initial chlorine dose, sewer video with no sag over 1/2 in, and 2 ft from storm drains and dry utilities.
field.title: Arizona MAG spec: which section covers what
field.topic: Arizona: MAG Uniform Standard Specifications and Details
field.source: MAG Uniform Standard Specifications and Details for Public Works Construction (Maricopa Association of Governments, Arizona), section map as referenced by Arizona utility construction guides; MAG is updated every year, check the edition

field.text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Section 33). A public gravity sewer carrying raw wastewater is not less than 8 inches in diameter (33.1). Sewers are designed for a mean velocity of at least 2.0 feet per second flowing full (33.41). Recommended minimum slopes, in feet per 100 feet: 8 inch 0.40; 10 inch 0.28; 12 inch 0.22; 15 inch 0.15; 18 inch 0.12; 21 inch 0.10; 24 inch 0.08 (the book's table goes on to 42 inch). Sewers 48 inches and larger are designed for at least 3.0 feet per second. Slightly flatter slopes can be allowed where the flow depth will be 0.3 of the diameter or more at design average flow (33.42). Installation (33.8): rigid pipe uses bedding Classes A, B, C or crushed stone as described in ASTM C12; flexible pipe uses embedment Classes I, II or III (ASTM D2321), carefully compacted; no debris, frozen material, large clods or stones, or organic matter in the final backfill within 2 feet of the top of the pipe (33.84). A crew does not pick the slope: lay to the plan grade, and flag it to the foreman or engineer if a plan grade is flatter than these.
field.title: Ten States Standards minimum sewer slopes by pipe size (8 inch = 0.40 percent) and 2 feet per second
field.topic: Sewer design standards: slopes, manholes, sizes
field.source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), 2014 edition, Sections 33.1-33.8 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: California Caltrans Standard Specifications (used on state highway work and by many Northern California cities): Section 19 earthwork covers excavation, embankment and structure backfill; relative compaction is tested by California Test 216 or 231; structure backfill around culverts and structures is typically compacted to at least 95 percent relative compaction, and embankment to 90 percent with 95 percent in the upper part of the roadbed (check the current section text for depths). Slurry cement backfill and CLSM are covered under structure backfill materials. Pipe culverts and drainage are in the 60s sections (61 culvert and drainage pipe joints, 64 plastic pipe, 65 concrete pipe, 66 corrugated metal pipe), and existing facilities in Section 15. Water and sewer work for cities usually follows the city's or district's own standard specs, not Caltrans.
field.title: California Caltrans specs for pipe and trench work: where to look
field.topic: California: Caltrans Standard Specifications
field.source: Caltrans Standard Specifications (California), Section 19 Earthwork and pipe sections; check the edition named in the contract

field.text: Missouri and Kansas cities in the Kansas City metro adopt the APWA Kansas City Metropolitan Chapter Construction and Material Specifications (including Section 2100 grading and site preparation and Section 2500 sanitary sewers) with their own amendments. Example amendments (Belton, Missouri, to Section 2500): trench widths by pipe size such as 22 in for 8 in pipe, 27 in for 12 in, 34 in for 18 in, 43 in for 24 in, 54 in for 30 in; pipe embedded in 1/2 in clean rock from 6 in below to 6 in over the pipe; under pavement, flowable fill (required in trenches 24 in wide or less) or dense-graded aggregate (KDOT AB-3 or MoDOT Type 5); no stones over 1 in in the first 12 in of backfill and none over 6 in anywhere; compaction tests each lift at every road crossing and every 50 ft under pavement; 9-arm mandrel (8 in SDR 35 mandrel 7.28 in, SDR 26 7.11 in); manhole vacuum test at 10 in Hg; CCTV of all new sewer. Check the base APWA KC section and your city's amendments.
field.title: Missouri and Kansas: APWA Kansas City Metro sanitary sewer spec (Section 2500), as adopted by cities
field.topic: Kansas City metro: APWA KC Metro Construction and Material Specifications
field.source: APWA Kansas City Metropolitan Chapter specifications Section 2500 as amended by the City of Belton, Missouri; check each city's adopted edition

field.text: Nevada, Las Vegas valley: work follows the Uniform Standard Specifications and Standard Drawings for Public Works Construction Off-Site Improvements, Clark County Area (latest edition), with Las Vegas Valley Water District and city standards. Example standard drawing for trench backfill in paved areas: at least 4 in of bedding; pipe zone (with bedding) of Type II aggregate base compacted to 90 percent of maximum density, or Class I CLSM (CLSM only for pipe larger than 24 in); aggregate base under the pavement section at 95 percent; drain rock stabilization up to 18 in deep where groundwater or poor subgrade; on wider streets a CLSM cap (12 in minimum for 60 to 80 ft right-of-way, 24 in for over 80 ft), not required on residential streets or trenches over 3 ft wide; backfill to subgrade minus 1 in; pavement replaced to existing depth plus 1 in per Uniform Standard Drawings 500 series; trench backfill above the pipe zone per Drawings 503 series. Check the current drawings and the agency's standards.
field.title: Nevada: Clark County (Las Vegas) trench backfill in paved areas
field.topic: Nevada: Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings
field.source: Clark County Area Uniform Standard Drawings (paved-area trench backfill sheet) and LVVWD standards (Nevada); check the latest edition

field.text: Federal law (the Fair Labor Standards Act) does not require meal or rest breaks for adults. If an employer gives short breaks (about 5 to 20 minutes), they count as paid work time (29 CFR 785.18). A bona fide meal period, usually 30 minutes or more, can be unpaid only if the worker is completely relieved of duty: someone told to stay with the machine, watch the trench or answer the radio while eating is working and must be paid (29 CFR 785.19). About 20 states add their own meal or rest break rules for adults; the rest follow the federal rule. Union agreements (CBAs) often set breaks and can replace state rules where the state law allows it. Breaks also tie into heat rules: water, shade and cool-down rest are required in states with heat standards. For the exact rule, check the state labor department; for a pay dispute, talk to HR or labor counsel.
field.title: Meal and rest breaks: the federal rule and how to find your state's
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: 29 CFR 785.18 and 785.19; U.S. DOL state break tables

field.text: Meal break laws for adults (general, as of 2026): roughly 20 states plus some territories. Paid rest break laws: about 9 states. If the job's state is not listed here, adults generally follow the federal rule (no required breaks; short breaks paid; off-duty meals of 30 minutes or more can be unpaid). States with a general adult meal-period law: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Kentucky, Maine, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nebraska (certain workplaces), Nevada, New Hampshire, New York, North Dakota, Oregon, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont (reasonable opportunity only), Washington, West Virginia; Maryland covers large retail only. States with paid rest-break laws: California, Colorado, Kentucky, Minnesota, Nevada, Oregon, Vermont, Washington, and Illinois (hotel room attendants only). Laws change: confirm with the state labor department.
field.title: Which states have their own adult break laws
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division state meal and rest period tables (rest table Jan 1, 2023); state labor departments

field.text: California break rules for adult employees. Construction is covered by IWC Wage Order 16 and Labor Code 512. Meal: a 30-minute off-duty meal must start before the end of the 5th hour of work (it can be waived by mutual consent if the whole day is 6 hours or less); a second 30-minute meal must start before the end of the 10th hour (it can be waived if the day is 12 hours or less and the first meal was not waived). Rest: a paid 10-minute rest for every 4 hours or major fraction, near the middle of each work period: none under 3.5 hours, 1 for 3.5 to 6 hours, 2 for over 6 to 10, 3 for over 10 to 14. So a 12-hour day needs 2 meals (the second can be waived only if the first wasn't) and 3 paid rests. A missed, late or interrupted meal or rest owes the worker 1 extra hour of pay at the regular rate per workday for each kind missed (Labor Code 226.7). The meal must be truly off duty: if the crew has to stay on site, watch equipment or stay on call, it's paid time. No rule adds time to the meal when the break area or trucks are far away. What counts is that the worker is relieved of all duty for the full 30 minutes and free to go where they want; walking to the truck on that free time is part of their own meal. If the employer keeps the crew on the jobsite during the meal (not allowed to leave), the meal is paid time even if they do no work (Huerta v. CSI Electrical Contractors, Cal. Supreme Court 2024). Construction employees under a qualifying union agreement can be exempt from the 512 meal rules (Labor Code 512(e)). Heat (section 3395): water, shade and cool-down rests whenever asked.
field.title: California: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Cal. Labor Code 512, 226.7; IWC Wage Order 16; Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court (2012); Huerta v. CSI Electrical Contractors (2024) (California)

field.text: Colorado break rules for adult employees. Colorado COMPS Order: a 30-minute uninterrupted, duty-free meal for shifts over 5 consecutive hours (if the work prevents a full break, an on-duty paid meal); paid 10-minute rest for every 4 hours or major fraction, in the middle of each period as practicable.
field.title: Colorado: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Colorado COMPS Order #39 (check current number) (Colorado)

field.text: Connecticut break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal for 7.5 or more consecutive hours, taken after the first 2 hours and before the last 2 hours. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Connecticut: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-51ii (Connecticut)

field.text: Delaware break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal for 7.5 or more consecutive hours, after the first 2 hours and before the last 2 hours; exceptions for union or written agreements and some small or single-person operations. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Delaware: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: 19 Del. C. 707 (Delaware)

field.text: Illinois break rules for adult employees. At least a 20-minute meal for 7.5 continuous hours, starting no later than the 5th hour (One Day Rest in Seven Act); union agreements may set different terms. Paid rest breaks are required only for hotel room attendants in large counties.
field.title: Illinois: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: 820 ILCS 140/3 (Illinois)

field.text: Kentucky break rules for adult employees. A reasonable meal period (usually 30 minutes) between the 3rd and 5th hour, plus a paid 10-minute rest for each 4 hours worked. Union or mutual agreements can modify.
field.title: Kentucky: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: KRS 337.355 and 337.365 (Kentucky)

field.text: Maine break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal opportunity after 6 consecutive hours, except in emergencies; small workplaces giving frequent paid breaks and union or written agreements can differ. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Maine: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: 26 M.R.S. 601 (Maine)

field.text: Massachusetts break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal, free of all duties and free to leave, for work over 6 hours in a day. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Massachusetts: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: M.G.L. c.149 s.100-101 (Massachusetts)

field.text: Minnesota break rules for adult employees. Enough time to eat a meal for 8 or more consecutive hours (unpaid if off duty; breaks under 20 minutes can't be deducted), and a paid rest period within each 4 consecutive hours to use the nearest restroom.
field.title: Minnesota: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Minn. Stat. 177.253 and 177.254 (Minnesota)

field.text: Nebraska break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal off the premises per 8-hour shift, for assembly plants, workshops and mechanical establishments; union or written agreements excluded. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Nebraska: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-212 (Nebraska)

field.text: Nevada break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal for 8 continuous hours, and a paid 10-minute rest for each 4 hours or major fraction (not required under 3.5 hours), for employers with 2 or more employees; union agreements excluded.
field.title: Nevada: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: NRS 608.019 (Nevada)

field.text: New Hampshire break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal after 5 consecutive hours, unless eating while working is practical and the employer allows it. No paid rest break law.
field.title: New Hampshire: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: RSA 275:30-a (New Hampshire)

field.text: New York break rules for adult employees. Shifts over 6 hours spanning 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. get a 30-minute noon meal (1 hour in factories); a shift starting before 11 a.m. and running past 7 p.m. gets another 20 minutes between 5 and 7 p.m.; shifts over 6 hours starting between 1 p.m. and 6 a.m. get a midway meal (45 minutes; 1 hour in factories). The Labor Commissioner can approve shorter periods. No paid rest break law.
field.title: New York: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: NY Labor Law 162 (New York)

field.text: North Dakota break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal for shifts over 5 hours when two or more employees are on duty (if the employee wants it); union agreements take precedence. No paid rest break law.
field.title: North Dakota: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: N.D. Admin. Code 46-02-07-02 (North Dakota)

field.text: Oregon break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute duty-free meal for each 6 to 8 hour work period (between the 2nd and 5th hour for periods of 7 hours or less, between the 3rd and 6th for longer), and a paid 10-minute rest for each 4 hours or major part, separate from the meal; union agreements excluded.
field.title: Oregon: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks

field.text: Rhode Island break rules for adult employees. A 20-minute meal in a 6-hour shift and 30 minutes in an 8-hour shift; small workplaces excluded. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Rhode Island: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: R.I. Gen. Laws 28-3-14 (Rhode Island)

field.text: Tennessee break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute unpaid meal for 6 or more consecutive scheduled hours, not before or during the first hour. No paid rest break law.
field.title: Tennessee: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: Tenn. Code 50-2-103(h) (Tennessee)

field.text: Vermont break rules for adult employees. No set length: employees must get reasonable opportunities during work periods to eat and use the toilet.
field.title: Vermont: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: 21 V.S.A. 304 (Vermont)

field.text: Washington break rules for adult employees. A 30-minute meal for work over 5 hours, starting between the 2nd and 5th hour (paid if the worker must stay on premises or on call), plus another 30 minutes for 3 or more hours past the normal workday; a paid 10-minute rest for each 4 hours, with no more than 3 hours worked without a rest. A union agreement covering construction trades can replace these if it specifically covers breaks.
field.title: Washington: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: WAC 296-126-092 (Washington)

field.text: West Virginia break rules for adult employees. A 20-minute meal for 6 or more consecutive hours where employees can't eat while working or don't get breaks. No paid rest break law.
field.title: West Virginia: meal and rest breaks
field.topic: Meal and rest breaks
field.source: W. Va. Code 21-3-10a (West Virginia)

field.text: For two forms (or boards) meeting at a corner, each piece is cut at half the turn: miter (from square) = (180 - corner angle) / 2. A 90 degree corner = 45 degree miter on each piece; 135 degree corner (a 45 degree bend) = 22.5; 120 degree = 30; 150 degree = 15. With vertical faces this is a plain miter (saw blade straight up). If the faces lean (battered curb face, sloped wall form), it becomes a compound cut: see the next entry. For a curb return or radius, use flexible forms (steel flex form, bender board, kerfed plywood) set to the radius from the center point instead of miters.
field.title: Miter angle for any corner of forms, curbs and walls
field.topic: Form and layout geometry
field.source: Standard carpentry and concrete forming practice

field.text: When the face of a form leans back (a battered curb face, a sloped wall), a 90 degree corner needs a compound cut: miter M = arctan(cos t) and blade bevel B = arcsin(sin t x sin 45), where t is the lean of the face from vertical (t = arctan(1 / run) for a batter of 1 in run). Saw settings for a 90 degree corner: batter 1:12 (1 in per ft), t 4.8, miter 44.9, bevel 3.4; batter 1:8, t 7.1, miter 44.8, bevel 5.0; batter 1:6 (2 in per ft), t 9.5, miter 44.6, bevel 6.7; batter 1:4 (3 in per ft), t 14.0, miter 44.1, bevel 9.9; batter 1:2, t 26.6, miter 41.8, bevel 18.4. For small batters (1:12) the bevel is only about 3 degrees, which is why many crews just cut plain 45s and accept a small gap. Other corner angles: M = arctan(cos t x tan(half the turn)), B = arcsin(sin t x sin(half the turn)). Cut a test pair from scrap first.
field.title: Compound miter for a battered curb face or sloped form at a 90 degree corner
field.topic: Form and layout geometry
field.source: Compound miter geometry (standard formulas for sloped-side frames)

field.text: 3-4-5: measure 3 along one line and 4 along the other; the diagonal is 5 when the corner is square (use 6-8-10, 9-12-15 or 12-16-20 for longer legs). Check a rectangle by its diagonals: equal diagonals = square. Diagonal of any rectangle = square root of (L squared + W squared). A curve from its radius: swing a tape from the radius point, or set points by offsets from the tangent: offset = R - square root (R squared - x squared) at distance x along the tangent. Arc length = R x angle (degrees) x 0.01745. Chord for a central angle = 2 R sin(angle / 2). Curb returns at intersections are often 25 to 35 ft radius; the plans or standard plan set the radius and the BC/EC points.
field.title: Laying out square corners, right angles and curves in the field
field.topic: Form and layout geometry
field.source: Standard field layout practice

field.text: A photo shows what's there, not true distances. A length can only be read from a photo when a known measure is in the frame and in the same plane: a tape laid along it, a grade rod, a lath, a standard brick or block. Angles and distances shrink with distance and tilt (perspective), so measurements from a photo are rough. Depths, elevations and slopes can't be read from a photo at all. Dimensions written on a plan, a stake or a tape in the photo can be read. When a needed number isn't readable, name exactly which one and where, and ask for a closer, straight-on photo of that spot.
field.title: What can and can't be measured from a photo
field.topic: Reading photos and plans
field.source: Standard practice

field.text: Read the written dimension, never scale the drawing unless the sheet says it is to scale and no dimension is given. Dimension strings add up to the overall: if one segment is missing, overall minus the others = the missing one. Check the scale bar (copies get resized). Know the notation: 12'-6" is 12 ft 6 in; 12.5' is decimal feet (civil plans use decimal feet: 0.5 ft = 6 in); dimensions to the face of stud, face of concrete, centerline or gridline are not the same. Plan notes and details override the general drawing; a revision cloud with a delta number shows a change. Pipe plans give station, offset, invert (IE), slope and pipe size; the profile shows depths and crossings.
field.title: Reading dimensions on plans and drawings
field.topic: Reading photos and plans
field.source: Standard plan reading practice

field.text: Locators write short codes next to their paint. Line type: E or ELEC electric, PRI primary (high voltage), SEC secondary, SL street light, TS or SIG traffic signal, G or GAS gas (HP high pressure, IP intermediate, LP low), OIL or PET petroleum, STM steam, T or TEL phone, FO fiber optic, CATV or TV cable, COMM communications, W water, FW or FIRE fire line, IRR irrigation, RW reclaimed, SS sanitary sewer, FM force main, SD storm drain, CO conduit, DB duct bank. Details: size (4", 2-4" for two lines), material (PVC, STL steel, PE, CI cast iron, DI, AC asbestos cement, CU copper), count (x3, 3 ducts), ABN abandoned, the owner's initials, depth if a private locator gave one (2.5'), a question mark for a suspected line, arrows for direction, T for a tee or branch, EOM or E/O end of marks, and NO, CLR or OK with an owner name meaning that owner has nothing in the area.
field.title: Abbreviations painted with locate marks
field.topic: Locate marks: codes and owners
field.source: APWA Uniform Color Code and common locator practice

field.text: Owner initials written with the paint name the utility that marked: for example AT&T, VZ (Verizon), LUMEN or CTL (CenturyLink), FTR (Frontier), SPEC or CHTR (Spectrum/Charter), CMCST (Comcast/Xfinity), COX, plus the local electric company or co-op, gas company, water district and city. The ticket (from the 811 center) lists every member notified for the dig site; the positive response system shows each member's answer (marked, clear, or no facilities). A line nobody marked may belong to no one on the ticket: private lines (on private property beyond the meter, parking lot lighting, irrigation, private sewer laterals) are not marked by 811 and need a private locator. When marks don't match the plans or a line has no owner, stop and call the 811 center for a re-mark or the owner.
field.title: Owner initials on locate marks and how to tell who owns a line
field.topic: Locate marks: codes and owners
field.source: 811 center and positive response practice; APWA color code

field.text: Surveyors set layout points in pavement as a nail, PK or MAG nail, drill hole or chiseled X, usually circled or boxed in paint with writing beside it. Paint color is often orange or pink, but any color is used: a nail in a painted circle is a survey point, not a utility locate. The writing reads like a stake: an offset over a line (10' over a bar or 10' O/S) to what the point is for: a building or column gridline (A, 3, A-3, ℄ COL), a building corner, property line (PL), right of way (R/W), centerline (℄ or CL), back or top of curb (BC/TC, but BC can also mean begin curve), edge of pavement (EP), a structure (MH, CB, VLT), plus a cut or fill and the grade it's to (FF finish floor, FS finish surface, FG finish grade, TW/BW top and bottom of wall). A long number nearby is often the point number from the surveyor's file. Leave the point alone and call the surveyor if it's hit or looks moved.
field.title: Reading survey layout paint on pavement and slabs
field.topic: Survey paint and layout marks
field.source: Common survey layout practice

field.text: A cut sheet lists every stake: point number, station, offset (distance and side, like 10' LT), what it's to (IE 8" SS, TC, FG, MH rim), the stake or hub elevation, the design elevation, and the cut or fill (hub minus design = cut when positive). Some add the slope, the distance to the next stake and notes. Use it to check the stake writing, set the grade rod or laser, and catch mistakes: the cut on the stake should match the sheet. If a stake and the sheet disagree, or an offset or station looks out of sequence, stop and call the surveyor. The sheet header gives the job, the date, the benchmark and datum used, and who set it.
field.title: Reading a cut sheet (grade sheet) from the surveyor
field.topic: Cut sheets and staking sheets
field.source: Common survey practice

field.text: A hot tap connects a new line to a main that stays in service. Steps (the water agency's spec governs): expose and clean the main, check the outside diameter and material, install a tapping sleeve (stainless or ductile iron, sized for the main's OD) and a tapping valve, support them, and pressure test the sleeve and valve before cutting (air or water, per the agency). The tapping machine bolts to the valve, cuts through the main and pulls out the coupon (keep it for the agency), then the valve is closed and the machine removed. A size-on-size tap needs a sleeve rated for it; many agencies limit tap size to one size smaller than the main. Thrust block or restrain the valve. Many agencies require their own crew or an approved contractor to tap.
field.title: Hot tap (live tap) on a water main
field.topic: Water and sewer tie-ins
field.source: AWWA M23 and M41; typical water agency standards

field.text: A cut-in needs a shutdown. The water agency schedules it, notifies customers (often 48 to 72 hours ahead), and usually operates the valves itself. Have every fitting, coupling, sleeve, pipe piece and pump on site before the shutdown, plus a plan to dewater the trench. Cut the main with a saw made for the material (never a torch on PVC; asbestos cement pipe needs AC-trained workers, wet cutting and disposal rules). Swab or spray the inside of every fitting and pipe piece with chlorine solution (AWWA C651 uses about 1 percent hypochlorite) and keep trench water out of the pipe. Install the tee or valve with solid sleeves or couplings, restrain, then the agency recharges slowly, flushes and may sample before customers are restored. New mains are normally pressure tested, disinfected and pass bacteria tests before the final connection.
field.title: Shutdown and wet tie-in (cut-in) on a water main
field.topic: Water and sewer tie-ins
field.source: AWWA C651 Disinfecting Water Mains; AWWA C600/C605; water agency standards

field.text: On a new main, laterals connect at a wye or tee (often 45 degree wye plus a 45 bend) set facing up at about 45 degrees. On an existing main, connect with a saddle or an insert tee in a cored hole (no breaking in with a hammer) per the agency. Common minimum lateral slope is 2 percent (1/4 in per ft) for 4 in and 6 in laterals; a cleanout at the property line or right of way is typical. A new pipe into an existing manhole: core drill and use a flexible boot (connector) and grout the channel; many agencies require an outside drop connection when the incoming pipe is more than about 2 ft above the manhole flowline. Plug and protect the existing flow while working, and check for gases before anyone enters the manhole (confined space rules).
field.title: Sewer lateral and manhole connections
field.topic: Water and sewer tie-ins
field.source: Typical agency sewer standards; ASTM C923 connectors

field.text: OSHA 1926.651(h): no one works in an excavation with accumulated water, or where water is accumulating, unless precautions protect them (special support or shield systems, water removal, safety harness and lifeline), and a competent person monitors the water removal. Methods: sump pumps in the trench for light seepage; well points (small wells on a header pipe along the trench) for sand and gravel with a high water table; deep wells or eductors for deep or tight soils. Pumping can wash fines out and undermine walls and nearby structures: watch for settlement and boils. Groundwater lifts empty pipe: keep dewatering until enough backfill is over it, or anchor it. A wet or soft trench bottom gets over-excavated and filled with crushed rock (often wrapped in filter fabric) per the engineer.
field.title: Dewatering a trench: methods and rules
field.topic: Dewatering
field.source: 29 CFR 1926.651(h); standard dewatering practice

field.text: Pumped water usually needs a permit to discharge: under the federal Clean Water Act, construction dewatering goes under the stormwater Construction General Permit or a state dewatering general permit, and discharging to a sanitary sewer needs the sewer agency's approval. Never pump muddy water straight into a storm drain, street gutter or creek: run it through a filter bag (dirtbag), settling tank (Baker tank) or sediment basin, and test or treat it if the site has known contamination (old fuel, solvents). Keep the permit, the sampling log and the SWPPP on site. Rules vary by state and city, so check the permit before you pump.
field.title: Where trench water can go: discharge permits and sediment control
field.topic: Dewatering
field.source: Clean Water Act NPDES; EPA and state construction general permits

field.text: Lift only with equipment rated for it: use the manufacturer's lift chart for that machine and attachment (capacity drops fast as the load moves out from the machine and over the side), use the rated lifting point (lift eye or hook on the bucket linkage, not the bucket teeth), and keep the load low. Excavators used as cranes may need load-holding valves and an overload warning per the manufacturer. Slings and hooks must be rated and inspected each shift (29 CFR 1926.251). Keep everyone out from under the load and out of the swing radius, use a tag line, and use one signal person. Check overhead power lines: stay at least 10 ft from lines up to 50 kV, more for higher voltage (29 CFR 1926.1408 and 1926.600).
field.title: Lifting pipe with an excavator or loader
field.topic: Equipment and rigging
field.source: 29 CFR 1926.251; 1926.600(a)(6); 1926.1408; manufacturer lift charts

field.text: Use nylon or polyester web slings, padded hooks or a spreader bar; never wire rope or chain directly on PVC, HDPE, coated steel or lined ductile iron. Lift long pipe with a spreader bar or two slings at about the quarter points so it doesn't bend. Don't drop, drag or roll pipe off a truck; unload with forks padded or slings. Store pipe on level supports, bells alternating, chocked so it can't roll, and keep PVC out of long sun exposure per the maker. Inspect each piece for gouges, cracks and damaged bells or gaskets before laying. Pipe makers' handling guides and AWWA manuals give limits.
field.title: Rigging and handling pipe without damaging it
field.topic: Equipment and rigging
field.source: AWWA M23 (PVC), M41 (ductile iron), M55 (PE); pipe manufacturer handling guides

field.text: Heavy equipment, spoil piles and trucks near the edge add load (surcharge) to the trench wall. OSHA requires spoil and equipment at least 2 ft back (or retaining devices) and that the protective system be designed for any surcharge loads. A common rule of thumb is to keep heavy equipment back at least a distance equal to the trench depth unless the shoring or shield is rated for it; the competent person and the protective system's tabulated data decide. Use barriers, stop logs or a spotter when trucks back up to an open trench, and never let a machine work across an unprotected trench edge.
field.title: Keeping equipment back from the trench edge
field.topic: Equipment and rigging
field.source: 29 CFR 1926.651(j)(2) and 1926.652; standard practice

field.text: Work zone traffic control follows the MUTCD (Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices), Part 6. The 11th Edition was published in December 2023, and states had 2 years to adopt it; cities add permit conditions. Taper length L in feet: L = W x S x S / 60 for speeds 40 mph or less, L = W x S for 45 mph or more (W = width of the offset in ft, S = speed limit or 85th percentile speed in mph). Merging taper at least L; shifting taper at least L / 2; shoulder taper at least L / 3; one-lane two-way (flagger) taper 50 to 100 ft; downstream taper 50 to 100 ft per lane. Channelizing devices are spaced about S ft apart in tapers and 2 x S ft along the work area. Example: 12 ft lane closure at 35 mph: 12 x 35 x 35 / 60 = 245 ft. Some states publish their own MUTCD edition or supplement (California and Texas do), which governs there.
field.title: Work zone traffic control: the MUTCD and taper lengths
field.topic: Traffic control (work zones)
field.source: FHWA MUTCD 11th Edition Part 6; state MUTCD editions

field.text: Typical advance warning sign spacing (the MUTCD sign spacing table, distances A, B, C between signs): urban low speed 100 ft each (the road agency sets the speed category; some state manuals set it by mph); urban high speed 350 ft; rural 500 ft; expressway and freeway 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,640 ft. Leave a longitudinal buffer space ahead of the work when possible. Flaggers: trained (many states require flagger certification), wearing high-visibility apparel (ANSI 107 Class 2 or 3), using a STOP/SLOW paddle, standing on the shoulder next to the lane they control or in the closed lane, where approaching drivers can see them in time, with an escape route; give the flagger a flagger-ahead sign in advance. Nighttime work needs lighting and retroreflective gear. The permit's traffic control plan governs on that job.
field.title: Advance warning signs, flaggers and buffer space
field.topic: Traffic control (work zones)
field.source: FHWA MUTCD 11th Edition Part 6; ANSI/ISEA 107

field.text: Before anyone enters a confined space or a live sewer or water structure (lift station wet well, valve or meter vault, manhole on a live line, tank, large pipe), stop and isolate everything that could start, flow, fill, pressurize or move while people are inside. In plain steps: 1) List every source: pumps and their floats or automatic start, force mains and check valves, gravity flow from upstream, bypass pumps, water or air lines, mixers and gates, electrical feeds, and water or pressure held behind a valve or plug. 2) Shut each one down the normal way. 3) Isolate it so it cannot come back on: open the disconnect and lock it (a control switch or float is not isolation); close valves and lock or tag them; for a line that could flood or gas the space, blank it, remove a section, or use double block and bleed (two closed valves locked or tagged, with the drain or vent between them open). 4) Release stored energy: bleed pressure, drain, block anything that can drop or turn. 5) Verify before entry: try to start the pump from its controls and confirm no pressure or flow. A lock physically stops a restart; a tag is only a warning. Good practice is a personal lock for each person going in, removed only by that person when they are out. A live sewer usually cannot be fully shut off upstream, so plugs, bypass, continuous air monitoring and a flow and weather watch are part of the plan. The entry permit lists the isolation used and the entry supervisor checks it before signing. Many owners and utilities operate their own valves and pumps: get their lockout done and confirmed. Plain-language guidance: your company program, the owner's procedure and the regulation govern.
field.title: Lockout before entry: isolate pumps, lines and power before anyone goes into a wet well, vault, manhole or live structure
field.topic: Lockout and isolation before entering a confined space or a live sewer or water structure
field.source: 29 CFR 1926.1202 (isolation, blanking, double block and bleed); 1926.1204(c)(3) and (e)(1); 1910.146(d)(3)(iii) and (f)(8); 1910.147(d); 1910.146 Appendix E

field.text: Construction crews entering a permit space work under 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA. The permit space program must include "isolating the permit space and physical hazard(s) within the space" (1926.1204(c)(3)). Isolation means entrants are completely protected against the release of energy and material into the space and contact with a physical hazard, by blanking or blinding, misaligning or removing sections of lines, pipes or ducts, a double block and bleed system, lockout or tagout of all sources of energy, blocking or disconnecting mechanical linkages, or barriers (1926.1202). Forced-air ventilation does not count as eliminating or isolating a hazard (1926.1203(g)), and alternate (ventilation-only) entry needs all physical hazards eliminated or isolated first (1926.1203(e)(1)). A plant's or utility's own staff (general industry) follow 1910.146: "isolating the permit space" (1910.146(d)(3)(iii)), with the isolation measures written on the permit (1910.146(f)(8)). OSHA's lockout/tagout standard 1910.147 (shutdown, isolation, lock or tag, stored energy, verify isolation) covers servicing and maintenance in general industry, not construction (1910.147(a)(1)(ii)(A)); on a construction job the electrical rule is 1926.417: deenergized equipment or circuits are rendered inoperative and tagged at every point where they can be energized. A sewer is different: OSHA says there is rarely any way to completely isolate a section of a continuous system (1910.146 Appendix E), so when isolation is infeasible the employer monitors continuously where entrants work and provides an early warning for engulfment (1926.1204(e)(1)). California: construction entries follow Title 8 section 1953(a)(3)(C) (isolating the permit space and physical hazards); general industry 5157(d)(3)(B) and (f)(8); and Cal/OSHA's lockout rule 3314: machinery stopped and its power source de-energized or disengaged (3314(c)) under a written hazardous energy control procedure (3314(g)). Plain-language summary, not the regulation; the regulation text and your company program govern.
field.title: Lockout before entry: which rules apply (OSHA 1926.1204(c)(3), 1910.146(d)(3)(iii), 1910.147, 1926.417; Cal/OSHA 1953, 5157, 3314)
field.topic: Lockout and isolation before entering a confined space or a live sewer or water structure

field.text: Alabama's dig law is Ala. Code Title 37, Chapter 15, with the Underground Damage Prevention Authority enforcing it. One center: Alabama 811. A 2026 rewrite (SB205) takes effect January 1, 2027; the notice and ticket-life numbers below are the same before and after. Notice: "at least two but not more than 10 working days prior to the start of the proposed excavation" (demolition or blasting: 2 working days to 30 calendar days). An excavation notice is "valid for a period of 20 working days from the proposed starting date" (demolition 30). Renew at least two working days before it expires. Premark the route or edges of the dig in white unless that would get in the way of traffic. Operators post a positive response; you may start early once all of them have. From January 1, 2027 the tolerance zone is the width of the line plus 18 inches on either side: find marked lines by noninvasive methods and keep 18 inches between any line and the cutting edge. Hit a line: notify the operator immediately.
field.title: Alabama 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Alabama 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Ala. Code 37-15-2, -4, -4.1, -4.2, -6, -8, -9, -10 as amended by 2026 SB205 (enrolled), effective Jan 1, 2027

field.text: Alaska's dig law is AS 42.30.400 to 42.30.490. One center: Alaska 811 (Alaska Digline). Notice: "at least two but not more than 15 working days" before digging. Remote locations: at least 10 but not more than 20 working days. The law sets no ticket expiry. The handbook says most owners treat a ticket as expired if more than 15 calendar days pass before digging starts (20 in remote places). Marks gone from weather, construction or vandalism: ask for a remark, give the old dig number, and plan on another 2 working days. Mark the dig area in white; "Black paint may be used when snow is on the ground." No digging until each line is field marked. Lines there but not located: call for a second request. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 2 feet on either side (30 inches for lines more than 10 feet deep). Hand dig or vacuum within 24 inches of a marked line. Hit a line: notify the utility and the one-call system right away; danger, clear out and call 911. Fines: $50 to $1,000 for each offense that causes or adds to damage.
field.title: Alaska 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Alaska 811, Alaska Digline)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Alaska 811 Excavator Handbook (2026) pp. 2-3, 6-8, 13-22; AS 42.30.400 to 42.30.490

field.text: Arizona's dig law is A.R.S. 40-360.21 to 40-360.32, enforced by the Arizona Corporation Commission. One center: Arizona 811. Mark the dig area with white lining before you call (40-360.22(C)); a person digging on a single-family home lot is excused. Operators must mark "as promptly as practicable, but not later than two working days"; Arizona 811 calls these two full working days, so a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day if every operator has answered. Working days skip Saturday, Sunday, legal holidays and the Friday after Thanksgiving. You may not start "before the location and marking are complete or the excavator is notified that marking is unnecessary." Marks are good for 15 working days from the date of marking. If work goes on, give notice at least 2 working days before they run out. Within 24 inches of a marked line, expose it carefully with hand tools and support it. Hit a line: tell the operator right away; gas or hazardous material, also call 911. Leave the hole open until the operator arrives. Fine: up to $5,000 per violation.
field.title: Arizona 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Arizona 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.text: Arkansas's dig law is the Arkansas Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Act, Ark. Code 14-271-101 and after. One center: Arkansas 811. Notice (14-271-112): "at least two (2), but not more than ten (10), full working days before commencing" the dig (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day). The notice is "effective for a period of twenty (20) working days from the date that the notice was given." Work not finished or marks gone: "reinitiate the notice procedure," which means calling it in again with the normal wait. The tolerance zone, white lining rule, damage steps and fine amounts were not read in this pass and are not confirmed here. Until they are: hand dig or vacuum to find any marked line before a machine works near it, and if you hit a line call the owner, and 911 if gas or liquid is escaping.

field.text: Colorado's dig law is C.R.S. 9-1.5-101 to 9-1.5-108, with the Underground Damage Prevention Safety Commission hearing violations. One center: Colorado 811. Notice: "at least two (2) full business days prior to any excavation," not counting the call day (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day). Marks are good for 30 days from the ticket's due date, or until you can't see them, whichever is first. To go on, notify Colorado 811 at least 2 business days before the 30 days end; once it has run out you need a new ticket. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Use non-destructive digging there (hand or vacuum). Check that every member on the ticket has posted a positive response before you dig. If one has not by the locate-by date, send an Excavator Re-Notification first. Hit a line: stop, notify 811 and the operator right away; gas release, clear the area and call 911.
field.title: Colorado 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Colorado 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.text: Connecticut's dig law is Conn. Gen. Stat. 16-345 to 16-359 with regulations R.C.S.A. 16-345-1 to 16-345-9. The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) oversees and enforces it. Call 811 (Call Before You Dig, CBYD). Notice: "at least two full days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, but not more than thirty (30) days" before digging. The app's table gives a 30-day ticket life from the regulation; that and the hand-dig distance were not on the page read today and are not confirmed here. Forgetting to call is not an emergency. An emergency excavation is one "necessary to correct an emergency involving danger to life, health, or property." Hit or touch a line: "Immediately and directly report the contact or damage to the affected public utility." For a gas escape or other danger, also alert emergency personnel (911) and keep people away. Violations can bring a civil penalty from PURA; the amount was not on the page.
field.title: Connecticut 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Call Before You Dig)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: R.C.S.A. 16-345-1 to 16-345-9 as described on the PURA "CBYD Current Provisions" page

field.text: Delaware's dig law is the Underground Utility Damage Prevention and Safety Act, 26 Del. C. chapter 8, enforced by the Public Service Commission. Call 811 (Miss Utility of Delmarva). Notice: "not less than 3 business days, but no more than 12 business days" before work begins. A ticket "is valid for 12 business days after the day on which the ticket is transmitted." "On the thirteenth day, the ticket will expire, and an update, remark, or new excavation ticket shall be required." "No excavation may begin until a positive response code of clear or no conflict or marked is received." Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outside wall or edge of the line. No mechanized equipment in it except to remove pavement; vacuum excavation is allowed; hand dig. White line marking is highly recommended when the exact location can't be given. Hit a line: report it to the owner immediately; dangerous gas or liquid escaping, call 911.
field.title: Delaware 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Miss Utility of Delmarva)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: 26 Del. C. 802, 803, 805, 806, 808, 810 (Underground Utility Damage Prevention and Safety Act; through 85 Del. Laws c. 345)

field.text: The District of Columbia's dig law is D.C. Code Title 34, Chapter 27. Call 811 (District One Call). Notice: at least 96 hours and not more than 10 days before work begins, not counting Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. A notice is good for 15 days, not counting weekends and legal holidays. Three days before that ends, or when marks can't be read, ask the one-call center for a re-mark; re-marking is done within 48 hours. No digging until the one-call center confirms the operators have answered (they have 72 hours). Marks are within 2 feet of the outermost part of the line. Within 18 inches of it, expose the line by hand digging. Hit a line: notify the operator immediately; gas or liquid release, also 911. No backfill over a damaged line without the operator's permission. Fines: $2,500 first violation, $5,000 second, $10,000 third or later.
field.title: District of Columbia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.edition: D.C. Code online, through D.C. Law 23-186 (2021)

field.text: Florida's dig law is chapter 556, the Underground Facility Damage Prevention and Safety Act. One center: Sunshine 811. Notice: "not less than 2 full business days before beginning any excavation" (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day) (10 full business days for underwater work). A ticket is valid for 30 calendar days. Not finished: give another notice for the part still to dig. Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outer edge of either side of the marked line. Inside it, "use increased caution": hand dig, pothole, soft dig or vacuum. You must check the positive responses before you dig. Pre-mark in white when the site can't otherwise be identified. Hit a line: "immediately notify the member operator"; if gas or a hazardous substance escapes, call 911. Citations are $500 plus court costs, $2,500 for hazardous material pipelines.
field.title: Florida 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Sunshine 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.text: Georgia's dig law is the Georgia Underground Facility Protection Act, O.C.G.A. 25-9, enforced by the Public Service Commission. One center: Georgia 811. Notice: the notice period starts at 7 AM on the first business day after Georgia 811 gets your request and runs at least 2 business days, so a Monday request is good to dig Thursday at 7 AM. A request after 4:30 PM counts as the next business day. You may start early only if every owner has already answered clear or marked. Check the Positive Response Information System (PRIS) before digging. A locate request is good for 30 calendar days. Georgia 811 allows a normal ticket to be updated two times (90 days); each update is a new ticket number. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on either side. Hit a line: stop, notify Georgia 811 and the owner; gas or hazardous liquid, call 911. Fines up to $10,000 per violation.
field.title: Georgia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Georgia 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.text: Hawaii's dig law is HRS chapter 269E, under the Public Utilities Commission. One center: the Hawaii One Call Center (811). Notice: "at least five working days but not more than twenty-eight calendar days prior to commencing excavation," except in an emergency. The center issues an inquiry identification number that "shall remain valid for not more than twenty-eight calendar days from the date of issuance." Ask to revalidate it before it expires; you must hold a valid number for the whole time you are digging. No notice is needed on private property owned only by the excavator where no operator has lines. The center notifies the operators the same day. The tolerance zone, hand-dig rule, damage steps and fine amounts are in other sections (269E-12 to 269E-14) that were not read in this pass and are not confirmed here.
field.title: Hawaii 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Hawaii One Call Center)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: HRS 269E-7 (capitol.hawaii.gov)
field.edition: HRS current edition online, read Nov 20, 2026
field.unconfirmed: tolerance zone, damage steps, fine amounts

field.text: Idaho's dig law is Idaho Code Title 55, Chapter 22, with the Damage Prevention Board hearing violations. Three centers answer 811: Dig Safe North Idaho 811 (Boundary, Bonner, Kootenai counties), North Idaho 811 (Benewah, Shoshone) and Digline (all other counties). Notice: "not less than two (2) business days nor more than ten (10) business days before the scheduled date." Marks you keep up are good for "no longer than four (4) consecutive weeks following the date of notification." If work has not started within three weeks, give notice again. An Update request extends an active ticket. Pre-mark the path of the dig in white paint. Do not dig "until all known facilities have been marked." Marks missing: send a Second request. Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outside edges of the line; find the line by hand digging there. Hit a line: notify the owner and the one-number service; danger, call 911 and clear the area. Report the damage to the Board.
field.title: Idaho 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Idaho Guide to Safe Digging 2026-27 (Damage Prevention Board, DOPL) pp. 4, 7, 9-12, 15-20, 29-36; Idaho Code 55-2201 to 55-2212

field.text: Illinois's dig law is the Underground Utility Facilities Damage Prevention Act, 220 ILCS 50, rewritten effective January 1, 2025 and enforced by the Illinois Commerce Commission. JULIE is the one-call center everywhere outside the City of Chicago; Chicago runs its own system (811 Chicago). Notice: "not less than 2 days but no more than 10 days in advance." A "day" skips Saturdays, Sundays, JULIE holidays and the day of the notice (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day). A normal notice is good for 25 days from the first request. An extension can be asked for from day 20 and adds 25 days. Pre-mark the dig area in white (black when there is snow on the ground). Since January 1, 2026: confirm every notified operator has posted a positive response before you dig. Tolerance zone: one and one-half feet (18 inches) on either side of the outside edge of the marked line. Hit a line: notify the owner and JULIE right away; gas or hazardous material escaping, call 911.
field.title: Illinois 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (JULIE; Chicago is separate)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.text: Indiana's dig law is Ind. Code 8-1-26, enforced by the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission. One center: Indiana 811. Notice: "at least two (2) full working days but not more than ten (10) calendar days before the commencement of the work." Work may start at 7 a.m. on the next working day after the two full working days, or sooner if every operator has posted an electronic positive response. (The Indiana 811 FAQ says 20 calendar days for the earliest call; the statute copy read says 10.) A notice "expires at 11:59 p.m. prevailing time twenty (20) days after the date the notice is received." Not finished: send a new locate request and wait for the operators to mark before going on. Indiana 811 calls it an Extension when the old marks can still be seen: you get a new ticket number and members get two full working days. White line the site when you can't give an address or highway location. Since January 1, 2025 every member must use Positive Response. No answer after two full working days: ask for an Additional (2nd) Notice. Damaging a pipeline after not calling or not white lining can bring a civil penalty up to $10,000. The tolerance zone was not confirmed today.
field.title: Indiana 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Indiana 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Ind. Code 8-1-26-16 (FindLaw copy, current as of Jan 1, 2026); Indiana 811 FAQ (Dec 11, 2024)
field.edition: FindLaw copy current as of January 1, 2026
field.unconfirmed: tolerance zone; earliest call (10 vs 20 calendar days)

field.text: Iowa's dig law is Iowa Code chapter 480; the Attorney General enforces it. One center: Iowa One Call. Notice: "at least forty-eight hours prior to the commencement" of digging, not counting the notice day, weekends and legal holidays. A ticket is "valid for twenty-five (25) calendar days beginning on the day the forty-eight-hour period concludes." There is no renewal: for a longer job, request a new locate ticket before the old one runs out. You can't dig on another excavator's ticket. Use white paint, flags or stakes to show the dig area unless it is clearly defined or you used electronic white-lining. Operators must post a positive response within the 48 hours. Check the Electronic Positive Response System before starting; if one is missing, contact the operator or Iowa One Call. Tolerance zone: 18 inches on either side of the line. Hand-dig test holes there; no machinery other than accepted methods such as vacuum excavation. Hit a line: tell the operator as soon as practical and do not backfill until it has looked; gas or liquid escaping, call 911.
field.title: Iowa 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Iowa One Call)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Iowa One Call Excavator Manual (July 2024) pp. 2, 12-19, 32-46, 54-56; Iowa Code ch. 480

field.text: Kansas's dig law is the Kansas Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act, K.S.A. 66-1801 to 66-1816, enforced by the Kansas Corporation Commission. One center: Kansas 811. Notice: "at least two full working days but not more than 20 calendar days before the scheduled excavation start date." (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day) The notice, or any update, is "valid for 20 calendar days after the excavation start date" (changed from 15 days on January 1, 2024). Ticket only what you can reasonably finish in that time. To go on, update the notice. Do not make repeated remark requests unless the cause was out of your control; the Commission has warned of fines for needless updates. Whiteline the dig area when the operator asks for it. Pre-engineered and permitted projects still need the notice before digging starts. The tolerance zone (24 inches in K.S.A. 66-1802) and fine amounts were not re-read today and are not confirmed here.
field.title: Kansas 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Kansas 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: K.S.A. 66-1804 (ksrevisor.gov, as amended eff. Jan 1, 2024)

field.text: Kentucky's dig law is the Underground Facility Damage Prevention Act, KRS 367.4901 to 367.4917. One center: Kentucky 811. Notice: "not less than two (2) full working days nor more than ten (10) full working days prior to commencing work" (a Monday call means Thursday is the first dig day). "Locate requests are valid for twenty-one (21) calendar days from the day of the initial request." Ask for remarking two working days before each 21-day period ends, or sooner if the marks are gone or the plan changes. Mark the edges of the dig yourself when an operator asks or the area can't be described. Operator did not respond in time: "the excavator shall submit a second notice." If there is still nothing one working day later, an excavator who followed the law is not liable for damage to lines that would have been located (not true for certain gas and hazardous liquid pipelines). Inside the tolerance zone, "hand-dig or use nonintrusive means." Machines are allowed for pavement, rock, and material more than 12 inches in any direction from the located line, with a watcher. Hit a line: stop and notify the operators; flammable, toxic or corrosive escape, call 911.
field.title: Kentucky 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Kentucky 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: KRS 367.4911 (Justia copy, effective Jan 1, 2022)

field.text: Louisiana's dig law is the Underground Utilities and Facilities Damage Prevention Law, R.S. 40:1749.11 to 1749.27 (amended effective August 1, 2026). One center: Louisiana 811. Notice (R.S. 40:1749.13): at least 48 hours and not more than 120 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays; the wait runs from 7:00 a.m. on the next working day after you call. Marks are good "as long as visible, but not longer than twenty calendar days, including weekends and holidays," from the mark-by time. Marks gone or work not done in time: give another notice to the center. Forestry, farm and marine digging: up to 30 calendar days. A notice designated a large project with a written agreement: 90 calendar days. Operators give a positive response through the center by the mark-by time; bad weather extends it. The marked location is the width of the line "plus eighteen inches on either side." Marks use the APWA color code. An excavator who called and followed the law is immune from civil liability to an operator that did not join the center or did not mark, unless the excavator was negligent. Fine amounts and the damage steps were not confirmed in this pass.
field.title: Louisiana 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Louisiana 811)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: La. R.S. 40:1749.14 (legis.la.gov; last amended by Acts 2026, No. 902, eff. Aug 1, 2026); R.S. 40:1749.13

field.text: Maine uses Dig Safe as its one-call center (call 811); the Public Utilities Commission enforces the state's Dig Safe law. Pre-mark the dig area in white (paint, flags, stakes or whiskers), then call at least 72 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays, and not more than 30 days ahead. Ticket life: tickets expire every 60 days. In every Dig Safe state a ticket expires if digging does not start within 30 days. Renew with at least 72 hours' notice (weekends and holidays not counted) so there is no gap; if the scope of work changes, get a new ticket instead. Whether a renewal prints a new number is not confirmed. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Hand dig or use vacuum equipment there; no machines until the line is verified. Power equipment may remove pavement only to the depth of the pavement. Dig Safe only notifies its members. Call non-member owners (often town water and sewer) yourself. Maine also has its own damage prevention statute, 23 M.R.S. 3360-A.
field.title: Maine 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Dig Safe)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
field.source: Dig Safe Excavator Manual (version Aug 2025; laws table updated 6/5/25) pp. 4-5, 9, 11, 14-19, 25-27, 31

field.text: Maryland's dig law is Public Utilities Article Title 12, Subtitle 1, enforced by the Maryland Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Authority. Call 811 (Miss Utility). Pick a start date "not sooner than 3 business days after the ticket is initiated" and not later than 12 business days after. Business days are Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, not holidays; a ticket taken after hours counts from the next business morning. "A ticket is valid for 12 business days after the selected start work date." If the work won't be done in that time, "repeat the notification" the same way as the first. Ticket Check (positive response) is mandatory for owner-members. Check it before digging: 866-821-4226 or online. Code 11 (critical facilities) is not a go-ahead. Emergency tickets: owners respond within two hours. The 18-inch hand-dig rule and fine amounts come from the statute, were not re-read today and are not confirmed here.
field.title: Maryland 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Miss Utility)
field.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone

field.edition: Miss Utility page as posted Nov 20, 2026
field.unconfirmed: 18-inch rule and fine amounts not re-read

field.text: Massachusetts uses Dig Safe as its one-call center (call 811); the Department of Public Utilities enforces the state's Dig Safe law. Pre-mark the dig area in white (paint, flags, stakes or whiskers), then call at least 72 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays, and not more than 30 days ahead. Ticket life: tickets expire 30 days from the day of issue. In every Dig Safe state a ticket expires if digging does not start within 30 days. Renew with at least 72 hours' notice (weekends and holidays not counted) so there is no gap; if the scope of work changes, get a new ticket instead. Whether a renewal prints a new number is not confirmed. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Hand dig or use vacuum equipment there; no machines until the line is verified. Power equipment may remove pavement only to the depth of the pavement. Dig Safe only notifies its members. Call non-member owners (often town water and sewer) yourself.
