field.text: Wisconsin uses its own manual, the 11th Edition Wisconsin MUTCD (WMUTCD). FHWA found it in substantial conformance with the national 11th Edition, and WisDOT uses the date of FHWA's letter, February 24, 2026, as its effective date. Wisconsin's Part 6 differences were not read here, so check the WMUTCD Part 6 before relying on a national number. Flaggers: Since January 1, 2020 all flaggers on Wisconsin state highways must be certified (training meeting the Wisconsin Flagging Handbook). (WisDOT Standard Specifications Section 104.6.1.2.2.) This wording is the state document as posted by the national Work Zone Safety Information Clearinghouse on 2022-08-02; confirm it in the current spec book before you rely on it. Tapers, sign spacing and cone spacing come from the national MUTCD Part 6 unless the state manual or the permit says otherwise: taper L = W x S x S / 60 at 40 mph or less and W x S at 45 mph or more. The approved traffic control plan governs.
field.title: Wisconsin traffic control: which MUTCD applies and the flagger training rule
field.topic: Traffic control: which manual applies and flagger cards
field.source: FHWA Wisconsin Division letter (Feb. 24, 2026) and WisDOT request on the 11th Edition WMUTCD

field.text: Wyoming: WYDOT's rules page shows the Transportation Commission adopting the 2009 MUTCD, with a Wyoming change that lets engineering judgment or an engineering study modify a Standard where site conditions make it impossible or impractical. Adoption of the 11th Edition was not confirmed from WYDOT; ask WYDOT Traffic which edition applies. Flaggers: Complete and pass a training program approved by the State Construction Office before flagging (3-day grace in unplanned emergencies); current card on the project. How long it lasts: tested every 3 years. Accepted: Wyoming Flaggers Traffic Control Certification, ATSSA. (WYDOT Standard Specifications Section 703.4.6.) This wording is the state document as posted by the national Work Zone Safety Information Clearinghouse on 2024-08-05; confirm it in the current spec book before you rely on it. Tapers, sign spacing and cone spacing come from the national MUTCD Part 6 unless the state manual or the permit says otherwise: taper L = W x S x S / 60 at 40 mph or less and W x S at 45 mph or more. The approved traffic control plan governs.
field.title: Wyoming traffic control: which MUTCD applies and the flagger training rule
field.topic: Traffic control: which manual applies and flagger cards
field.source: WYDOT Standards for Uniform Traffic Control Devices page (Transportation Commission resolution)
field.edition: 2009 MUTCD as adopted by the Wyoming Transportation Commission

field.text: California's Table 6B-1 in the CA MUTCD 2026 sets advance warning sign spacing by speed on urban streets, which the national table does not. Distances A, B and C are the same within each row. Urban, 25 mph or less: 100 ft. 30 mph: 150 ft. 35 mph: 200 ft. 40 mph: 250 ft. 45 mph: 300 ft. Urban, 50 mph or more: 350 ft. Rural: 500 ft. Expressway or freeway: A 1,000 ft, B 1,500 ft, C 2,640 ft. A is from the taper or point of restriction to the first sign, B from the first to the second sign, C from the second to the third. Use the posted speed limit, the off-peak 85th-percentile speed before work starts, or the expected operating speed. So three signs on a 35 mph city street sit 200 ft apart, 600 ft in all. These are recommended minimums; the encroachment permit or the approved traffic control plan can ask for more, and on State highways the Caltrans Standard Plans govern.
field.title: California advance warning sign spacing by speed (CA MUTCD Table 6B-1)
field.topic: Traffic control: advance warning signs
field.source: CA MUTCD 2026 (Caltrans, eff. Jan. 18, 2026), Table 6B-1 and footnotes; Section 6B.04

field.text: California's CA MUTCD 2026 prints the taper lengths for a 12 ft offset in Table 6B-3(CA). Merging taper L, then shifting taper L/2, then shoulder taper L/3, in feet. 20 mph: 80, 40, 27. 25 mph: 125, 63, 42. 30 mph: 180, 90, 60. 35 mph: 245, 123, 82. 40 mph: 320, 160, 107. 45 mph: 540, 270, 180. 50 mph: 600, 300, 200. 55 mph: 660, 330, 220. 60 mph: 720, 360, 240. 65 mph: 780, 390, 260. 70 mph: 840, 420, 280. 75 mph: 900, 450, 300. Downstream taper: 50 ft, 100 ft maximum. For another width use the formula: W x S x S / 60 at 40 mph or less, W x S at 45 mph or more. S is the posted speed limit, the off-peak 85th-percentile speed before work starts, or the expected operating speed. Devices in the downstream taper and in the one-lane two-way taper go about 20 ft apart. On State highways use the Caltrans Standard Plans for traffic control systems, T9 to T27 (Section 6B.08).
field.title: California taper lengths by speed for a 12 ft lane (CA MUTCD Table 6B-3(CA))
field.topic: Traffic control: tapers and buffer spaces
field.source: CA MUTCD 2026, Section 6B.08 paras. 4, 8, 12, 14, 16; Tables 6B-3, 6B-3(CA), 6B-4

field.text: California does not issue a state flagger card, but training is mandatory. The CA MUTCD 2026 adds a California Standard to Section 6D.01: flaggers shall be trained in the proper fundamentals of flagging moving traffic before being assigned as flaggers. The training covers nine topics, among them flagger equipment, the layout of the work zone, signaling to stop, proceed and slow, one-way traffic control, emergency vehicles, handling emergencies, hostile drivers, and flagging alone. The trainer shall have the qualifications and experience to teach it, and the employer shall keep the training records required by its Injury and Illness Prevention Program (8 CCR 3203). The Cal/OSHA rule is Construction Safety Orders section 1599. Paddle: a 24 by 24 inch STOP/SLOW paddle may be used where more emphasis is needed and speeds are 30 mph or more; on a staff, the bottom of the paddle should be at least 6 ft above the pavement. Flags are for emergencies, at least 24 inches square. Apparel is ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 Class 2 or 3, Class 3 recommended for flaggers at night (Section 6C.05). Flagger stations shall be lit at night except in emergencies.
field.title: California flagger training rule and paddle (CA MUTCD 6D.01, 8 CCR 1599)
field.topic: Traffic control: flaggers
field.source: CA MUTCD 2026, Sections 6D.01 paras. 2-5, 6D.02 paras. 4, 5a, 6D.03, 6D.06 para. 5, 6C.05; 8 CCR 1599, 3203

field.note: Vehicle Code text read on a third-party mirror (california.public.law); confirm on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov.
field.text: California Vehicle Code 42009 raises the penalty for listed moving violations in a highway construction or maintenance area: a misdemeanor fine is doubled, and an infraction is charged one category higher on the uniform traffic penalty schedule. It applies only when workers are actually doing the work and traffic control devices or warning signs tell drivers the workers are there. The listed offenses include speeding, obeying traffic devices, passing, right-of-way, turning, reckless driving and DUI. Speed zones: the CA MUTCD 2026 (Section 6B.01) says a reduced construction speed limit under Vehicle Code 22362 has to be documented in writing, cannot be set below 25 mph, is posted only where the work affects traffic, and the signs are covered or removed in non-working hours unless the condition is still there. Vehicle Code 21367 lets the agency doing the work regulate traffic through it. The contractor cannot post a regulatory speed limit on its own; the agency orders it.
field.title: California work zone fines and construction speed zones (CVC 42009, 22362)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines
field.source: Cal. Veh. Code 42009(a)-(c); Veh. Code 22362, 21367; CA MUTCD 2026 Section 6B.01 paras. 19a, 20c-20p
field.edition: Cal. Veh. Code 42009 as read 2026-11-20; CA MUTCD 2026

field.text: Arizona doubles the cost of speeding in a state highway work zone when workers are present. A.R.S. 28-710: in a state highway work zone marked by traffic control devices that show where it begins and ends, a driver may not exceed the speed shown on the devices; if workers are present, the driver pays the normal civil penalty plus an additional assessment equal to it. Half of the extra goes to the state highway work zone safety fund and half to the state highway fund. Signs: the Arizona Supplement to the MUTCD (Section 6G.08) says double fine signs in state highway work zones go up only when workers are present and come down or are covered when they are not, existing speed limit signs inside the double fine area are covered, and the layout should follow the ADOT Temporary Traffic Control Design Guidelines. Leaving the double fine signs up with no crew there is not allowed under that section. City streets are not state highway work zones under this statute.
field.title: Arizona work zone double fines (A.R.S. 28-710) and the signs
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines
field.source: A.R.S. 28-710(A)-(D); A.R.S. 28-652; ADOT Arizona Supplement to the MUTCD 11th Edition (Jan. 2026) Section 6G.08

field.note: Read on nevada.public.law (mirror, accessed text dated May 2025); confirm on leg.state.nv.us.
field.text: Nevada adds a second penalty, equal to the first, for speeding and other listed traffic offenses in a temporary traffic control zone (NRS 484B.130). It applies when construction, maintenance or repair workers are present, or when the road condition, such as narrowed or shifted lanes or an uneven surface, makes the violation more dangerous. The added penalty is capped at $1,000, 6 months in jail or 120 hours of community service. Signs are part of it: the agency or its contractor must put up a sign before the zone reading DOUBLE PENALTIES IN WORK ZONES, a sign at the beginning of the zone and a sign at the end. If the signs are missing the double penalty generally does not apply, unless the violation injured a worker or did $1,000 or more in property damage. Signs are not required for emergency zones or on roads posted 25 mph or less next to residential areas, and there the double penalty applies only with a worker injury or $1,000 or more in damage. So on a Nevada job, the three signs are the contractor's to set.
field.title: Nevada double penalties in work zones (NRS 484B.130)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines

field.note: Read on FindLaw (current as of 2026-01-01); confirm on statutes.capitol.texas.gov.
field.text: Texas Transportation Code 472.022 makes it an offense to disobey a warning sign or drive around a barricade, with a fine of $1 to $200. If it happens in a construction or maintenance work zone while workers are present, and the citation says so, the fine is $2 to $400. A stretch of road only counts as a construction or maintenance work zone for this purpose if it is marked by signs that say it is a work zone, show where the zone begins and ends, and state: Fines double when workers present. Mobile operations, as the Texas MUTCD defines them, are not included. Driving around a barricade placed because water is over the road is a Class B misdemeanor. For a crew this means the begin, end and fines-double signs have to be in the setup for the higher fines to apply.
field.title: Texas work zone fines double when workers are present (Transp. Code 472.022)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines
field.source: Tex. Transp. Code 472.022
field.edition: Tex. Transp. Code 472.022, current as of Jan. 1, 2026

field.text: Florida doubles the speeding fine in a posted construction zone under section 318.18(3)(e), Florida Statutes. Two conditions: the zone is posted, with the posting stating the speed limit and that fines are doubled; and construction personnel are present or operating equipment on the road or immediately next to it. The regular fines in 318.18(3)(b) are $25 for 6 to 9 mph over, $100 for 10 to 14 over, $150 for 15 to 19 over, $175 for 20 to 29 over and $250 for 30 mph or more over, so doubled they are $50, $200, $300, $350 and $500, before court costs. No crew on or beside the road means no doubling, even with the signs up. FDOT work zone layouts are in the FDOT Standard Plans, Index 102 series, and FDOT requires its Temporary Traffic Control (MOT) training for people who set up and supervise work zones on state roads; those two points were not confirmed from an FDOT page here.
field.title: Florida speeding fines double in a posted construction zone (s. 318.18(3)(e))
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines

field.text: Washington requires a flagger card by state safety rule. WAC 296-155-305(6): each flagger must have in their possession a valid Washington traffic control flagger card, or a valid card from a state that has a reciprocity agreement with Washington. The card shows the training completed, the date, the instructor, the issuing state and an expiration date no more than 3 years from issue, with a photo or the words valid with photo ID. Training is based on the MUTCD. The reciprocity states named are Oregon, Idaho and Montana, and the WSDOT standard specifications (1-10.3(1)A) likewise accept cards from those states. Someone without a card may flag only in an emergency, until a certified flagger takes over. Other points in the same rule: flaggers are used only when other traffic control is not enough; the employer orients each flagger to the site (the job, equipment, traffic pattern, signals with operators, an escape route on foot); a site-specific traffic control plan is kept on site for jobs longer than one day; flaggers may not be given other duties or use a cell phone or headphones while flagging; and they get a paid 10 minute rest for each 4 hours.
field.title: Washington flagger card rule (WAC 296-155-305)
field.topic: Traffic control: flaggers
field.source: WAC 296-155-305(2), (6), (7), (9); WSDOT Standard Specifications 1-10.3(1)A

field.text: Washington doubles the penalty for speeding in a roadway construction zone. RCW 46.61.527: a roadway construction zone is an area where public employees or private contractors are doing construction, repair or maintenance work on or next to a public road. A driver may not exceed the speed shown on the traffic control devices in the zone, and a speed infraction there carries twice the usual penalty, which may not be waived, reduced or suspended. The same section creates the crime of reckless endangerment of roadway workers, a gross misdemeanor: driving in a construction zone in a way that endangers or is likely to endanger people or property, or removing, evading or intentionally striking a traffic safety or control device. A conviction brings a 60 day license suspension. Standards for the devices on state highways are set by the Secretary of Transportation. The text read here showed amendments through 2009; later changes were not confirmed.
field.title: Washington speeding in a roadway construction zone: double penalty (RCW 46.61.527)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines

field.text: Oregon's standard for short work zones is the Oregon Temporary Traffic Control Handbook, 2026 edition (January 2026), adopted through OAR 734-020-0005. It covers traffic control in place continuously for three days or less on any public road in the state. Longer jobs, or jobs more complicated than the handbook's diagrams, need a full traffic control plan. A traffic control plan is required whenever work is done on or along a public road; for short jobs the handbook diagram can be the plan. Flaggers: certified in Oregon, Washington, Idaho or Montana, at least 18 years old, retrained every three years, carrying the card (sections 3.2 and 3.3). When only flaggers are used, the distance between the Flagger signs should not be more than one mile; past that use a pilot car. Drivers should not be held longer than 20 minutes at a flagger station under normal conditions. Apparel: ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 or later, Type R, Class 2 or 3; flaggers Class 2 required and Class 3 recommended at night. Cone spacing: the posted speed in feet in a taper and twice that along the work. Cities and counties may be stricter and usually require a permit.
field.title: Oregon Temporary Traffic Control Handbook (OTTCH): the rules for jobs of 3 days or less
field.topic: Traffic control: which manual applies and flagger cards
field.source: Oregon Temporary Traffic Control Handbook 2026 (ODOT), sections 1.1, 1.4, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 3.6, 3.8; OAR 734-020-0005

field.text: Colorado increases penalties and surcharges for listed traffic violations inside a designated maintenance, repair or construction zone (C.R.S. 42-4-614, with the amounts in 42-4-1701(4)(c)). CDOT designates the zone on a state highway; on any other road the public entity doing the work does. A zone can be designated only when work is going on or will be within four hours. Signs make the zone: one sign before the work area telling drivers that increased penalties are in effect, and one after it telling them the increased penalties no longer apply. The zone runs from the first sign to the second. The signs must meet CDOT's requirements and may be on fixed, variable or movable stands, or on a moving vehicle for work such as striping. The size of the increase was not confirmed here; it is set in section 42-4-1701. Colorado flagger notes from CDOT: flaggers must speak and understand English, and fluorescent red apparel is not allowed for flaggers.
field.title: Colorado work zone penalties and the signs that turn them on (C.R.S. 42-4-614)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines
field.source: C.R.S. 42-4-614; C.R.S. 42-4-1701(4)(c); CDOT Flagger Program industry memo (Jan. 1, 2026)

field.text: Utah Code 41-6a-209 does two things. First, it is an offense to willfully fail or refuse to obey a lawful order or direction of a flagger at a highway construction or maintenance site who is using the devices and procedures required, the same as disobeying a peace officer or a school crossing guard. Second, for speeding in a highway construction or maintenance site, the court must set the fine at no less than double the amount in the uniform recommended fine schedule, but only if workers are present at the site and the site is clearly marked with signs warning drivers of the doubled fine. Without workers there, or without the signs, the doubling does not apply. Flaggers in the state must be trained and certified before flagging, and the certification lasts three years (UDOT Flagger Training and Certification page). The section's last listed amendment is from the 2005 General Session; later changes were not confirmed.
field.title: Utah: obey the flagger, and double fines for speeding past workers (41-6a-209)
field.topic: Traffic control: work zone speed and fines
field.source: Utah Code 41-6a-209; UDOT Flagger Training & Certification page

field.note: Read through the WebFetch summarizer (the ATMS PDF is 580k characters); numbers match the national table pattern. Confirm in the printed ATMS before a crew sheet uses them.
field.text: Alaska's 2026 Alaska Traffic Manual Supplement (ATMS), effective January 20, 2026, changes a few national Part 6 numbers. Advance warning sign spacing (ATMS Table 6B-1, which replaces the national table): urban low speed 100 ft between signs, urban high speed 350 ft, rural 500 ft, expressway or freeway A 1,000 ft, B 1,500 ft, C 2,640 ft. The footnote sets low speed as 40 mph or less and high speed as 45 mph or more. Flagger paddle (6D.02): at least 24 inches wide with 8 inch letters, except on local roads with a speed limit of 25 mph or less, where 18 inches with 6 inch letters is allowed. Flagger certification (6D.01): on state highways flaggers must be certified under the current Standard Specifications for Highway Construction, Section 643, Traffic Maintenance. Speed reductions in the work zone (6B.01): avoid them where practical, keep them to 10 mph or less unless restrictive features require more, and follow DOT&PF Policy and Procedure 05.05.020. The approved traffic control plan or permit governs.
field.title: Alaska work zone sign spacing, flagger paddle and flagger certification (2026 ATMS)
field.topic: Traffic control: advance warning signs
field.source: 2026 ATMS Rev. 0 (Alaska DOT&PF), Sections 6B.01 paras. 17-19A, 6D.01 para. 01A, 6D.02 para. 02A, Table 6B-1

field.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-04.3(1), storm sewers). Exfiltration test: leakage no more than 1 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet, with at least 6 feet of water above the crown; the allowance rises 10 percent for each extra 2 feet of head, and pressure at the low-end invert is capped at 16 feet of water (7-04.3(1)B). Infiltration test: no more than 0.8 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet (7-04.3(1)C). Low-pressure air test: the pressure-drop time must be at least the table time, for example 80 seconds for 100 feet of 12-inch pipe; pipe that does not pass air (plastic, lined) needs four times the table time; pipe over 30 inches is tested joint by joint under ASTM C1103 (7-04.3(1)E and F). Sanitary sewers are stricter: see Section 7-17.
field.title: Washington WSDOT storm sewer tests (Section 7-04)
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition). Manholes, inlets and catch basins (7-05): dig to leave 1 foot clear between the structure and the bank; ladder rungs at 12 inches; rigid pipe entering a sanitary manhole needs a flexible joint within 1.5 pipe diameters or 18 inches of the wall, whichever is greater; manholes over 10 feet are paid per extra foot; an abandoned manhole is broken down to at least 4 feet below the new surface and filled with sand compacted to 90 percent. Side sewers (7-18): joint deflection never more than 2 inches per foot, use 1/8 bends for bigger turns; a 6-inch test tee goes where the side sewer crosses the right-of-way line; mark the end with a 2x4 stake 4 feet long buried 3 feet. Cleanouts (7-19): at each total 90 degrees of change in grade or alignment, never more than 100 feet apart, same size as the side sewer.
field.title: Washington WSDOT manholes, catch basins, side sewers and cleanouts (Sections 7-05, 7-18, 7-19)
field.topic: Spec books: manholes, inlets and catch basins
field.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 400, Excavation and Backfill for Structures: pipe gets Class C bedding unless the plans show something else; for precast concrete pipe the ASTM C1479 beddings are allowed (400.3.2). Pipe backfill goes in uniform layers no more than 8 inches deep (loose), each lift compacted mechanically, with the haunches thoroughly compacted (400.3.3.3); each layer must meet the density required for the roadbed (400.3.3.1; the percent comes from the embankment item and the plans, not Item 400). Cement-stabilized backfill: at least 7 percent cement by dry weight of aggregate, placed and compacted within 2 hours of mixing (400.3.3.4). Flowable backfill (Item 401, Table 2): excavatable mix 80 to 200 psi at 28 days; non-excavatable over 200 psi. Trench protection (Item 402): furnish and place excavation protection for trenches 5 feet or greater in depth, following OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P.
field.title: Texas TxDOT pipe excavation, bedding and backfill (Items 400, 401, 402)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: TxDOT Standard Specifications for Construction and Maintenance of Highways, Streets, and Bridges, 2024, Items 400, 401, 402 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 464, Reinforced Concrete Pipe: circular pipe Classes I through V (D-loads 800 to 3,000); joints may be mortar, cold-applied asphalt joint compound, rubber gaskets (ASTM C1619 Class A or C) or preformed flexible sealant (ASTM C990); arch and elliptical pipe need at least 1 foot of cover; do not run heavy earth-moving equipment over the pipe until at least 4 feet of compacted fill is in place unless the plans or the Engineer allow it in writing (464.3.1). Item 460, Corrugated Metal Pipe: lay from the outlet end with laps pointing upstream; same 4-foot rule for heavy earth-moving equipment (460.3.2); bell-and-spigot gaskets to ASTM F477 with at least a 6-inch stab depth. Item 462, Concrete Box Culverts: no more than four lifting holes per precast section, each 3 inches or smaller; boxes with joints that are not mortar can be backfilled right away. Jacking, boring or tunneling any of these is under Item 476.
field.title: Texas TxDOT concrete pipe, metal pipe, box culverts; fill before equipment crosses new pipe (Items 460, 462, 464)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Items 460, 462, 464 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications, Item 468, Thermoplastic Pipe). Bedding at least 4 inches thick, 6 inches where large rocks are present (468.3). Granular backfill goes in uniform loose layers about 6 inches deep up to 12 inches above the pipe; within 12 inches of the pipe use only hand-operated tampers; with flowable backfill the trench is pipe outside diameter plus 12 inches, the fill is carried at least 12 inches above the pipe, and you wait 24 hours before backfilling the rest (468.3.11). Stop backfilling if measured deflection passes 5 percent. No heavy earth-moving equipment over the pipe until at least 4 feet of compacted fill is in place (468.3.12). Final inspection (468.4.1): at least 30 days after backfill is complete, pull a mandrel sized at 95 percent of the pipe diameter through the whole length; if it will not pass, a 92.5 percent mandrel is tried and a remote camera is used to look at joints, cracks, deflection and ponding. Pipe deflected more than 7.5 percent of nominal diameter must be fixed or replaced (468.4.2). Joints: the bell must overlap at least two corrugations of the spigot.
field.title: Texas TxDOT thermoplastic pipe (HDPE, PP, PVC): backfill, mandrel and deflection limits (Item 468)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Item 468 Thermoplastic Pipe (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 476, Jacking, Boring, or Tunneling Pipe or Box: line and grade may not vary more than 1 inch in 10 feet; over-excavation no more than 2 inches at the top and sides, and anything over 1 inch is pressure grouted; do not excavate more than 2 feet ahead of the pipe; keep jacking going without interruption so the pipe does not set up; parallel jacked or tunneled lines need at least 3 feet clear between them; use plywood cushions between pipe ends, 1/2 inch minimum for pipe 30 inches and smaller and 3/4 inch for larger pipe and boxes; boring starts with a 2-inch pilot hole; keep a 3:1 slope from the edge of pavement on the shaft side. Item 465, Junction Boxes, Manholes, and Inlets: structures with rubber boots, gaskets or preformed sealant joints can be backfilled right away; place and compact backfill so the structure does not move. Item 479, adjusting manholes and inlets: flexible extension rings no taller than 3 inches; when capping, remove the structure to at least 1 foot below subgrade. Item 471 castings are load tested at 40,000 lb on a 9 by 9 inch block for 1 minute.
field.title: Texas TxDOT jacking, boring and tunneling pipe; manholes and inlets (Items 476, 465, 479)
field.topic: Spec books: jacking, boring and tunneling
field.source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Items 465, 471, 476, 479 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: California (Caltrans 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 19 Earthwork). Structure backfill, which is what goes around culverts and drainage structures: layers no more than 0.67 foot (8 inches) thick before compacting; relative compaction at least 95 percent; at least 90 percent is allowed at overside drains, headwalls, endwalls, culvert wingwalls and similar spots with nothing under pavement (19-3.03E(1)). Ponding and jetting is allowed only where the backfill drains freely and the foundation will not soften, in layers up to 4 feet, never in the top 4 feet below finished grade, and with vibratory compaction added. Slurry cement backfill: at least 188 lb of cement per cubic yard, placed within 1 hour of mixing, and nothing placed over it for at least 4 hours (19-3.02E, 19-3.03F). Soil cement bedding: at least 282 lb of cement per cubic yard and an 8-hour wait (19-3.02F(3), 19-3.03H). Embankment (19-5): 95 percent for 0.5 foot below the grading plane and 2.5 feet below finished grade under the traveled way plus 3 feet each side; 90 percent elsewhere. Caltrans 'relative compaction' is by California Test 216/231, not Proctor.
field.title: California Caltrans structure backfill and compaction numbers (Sections 19-3, 19-5)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: Caltrans Standard Specifications, 2025, Sections 19-3 and 19-5 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: California (Caltrans 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 61, Drainage Facilities, general). Pipe materials have their own sections: plastic pipe Section 64, concrete pipe Section 65, corrugated metal pipe Section 66. Watertight joints are proven by holding a 10-foot head of water above the pipe crown for 10 minutes (61-2.01D(2)(b)). Field leak testing is done on culverts and drainage structures only where the plans show it (61-2.01D(3)(a)); the low-pressure air test is not used on drainage pipe over 30 inches (61-2.01D(3)(c)). Concrete backfill in pipe trenches is consolidated with high-frequency internal vibrators, and with rapid-strength concrete nothing goes on top until it reaches 500 psi (61-5.03). For plastic pipe in saturated clay, unsuitable material is removed at least 1/4 of the pipe diameter, and not less than 6 inches, each side of the pipe. Not confirmed here: Caltrans minimum cover for construction loads and plastic pipe deflection limits (Sections 64 to 66); read the section or the plans.
field.title: California Caltrans drainage pipe joints and leak tests (Section 61)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Caltrans Standard Specifications, 2025, Section 61 Drainage Facilities (read 2026-11-20; sections 64-66 not read)

field.text: Colorado (CDOT 2025 Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Section 206, Structure Excavation and Backfill). Structure backfill is Class 1 or Class 2, or Flow-Fill. Each layer of backfill is 6 inches or less. Both classes are compacted to at least 95 percent of maximum dry density, within plus or minus 2 percent of optimum moisture (soils with more than 35 percent passing the No. 200 sieve at 0 to 3 percent above optimum). Maximum density is by AASHTO T 180 for Class 1 and for A-1, A-2-4, A-2-5 and A-3 soils, and by AASHTO T 99 (as modified by CP 23) for other Class 2 materials (206.03). Flow-Fill is not compacted and goes in lifts of 3 feet or less unless the Engineer approves more; the next lift waits until the surface dents less than 3 inches with no visible water (ASTM D6024). Do not backfill against new concrete until it reaches 0.8 f'c. Bed course material is per 703.07 (206.02(b)).
field.title: Colorado CDOT structure backfill and compaction (Section 206)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: CDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025, Section 206 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Colorado (CDOT 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 603, Culverts and Sewers). Bedding: a layer of loose structure backfill at least 3 inches thick (603.05). In new embankment, build the fill to at least 0.3 times the pipe outside diameter or rise before trenching for the pipe. Storm drain joints must be watertight; sanitary sewer concrete pipe uses rubber gaskets (603.07). Deflection of metal and plastic pipe: 5 percent maximum, measured 30 days or more after installation with a mandrel, laser profile or another approved method; replaced pipe is retested after another 30 days (603.10). Reinforced concrete pipe gets a visual inspection per AASHTO LRFD Section 27.6. Sanitary sewer leak limit: no more than 0.6 gallon per inch of inside diameter per 100 feet per hour (603.09). Jacked pipe: no trenching; grout the outside with 1 part portland cement to 3 parts fine aggregate. Section 604, manholes and inlets: a manhole in pavement is not built to final grade until the paving is done; pay depth is in 5-foot steps (0 to 5.0 ft pays as 5, 5.1 to 10.0 as 10).
field.title: Colorado CDOT culverts and sewers: bedding, joints, 5 percent deflection, leak test (Sections 603, 604)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: CDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025, Sections 603 and 604 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Chapter 30, Design of Sewers). Many state environmental agencies review sewer plans against this book or their own version of it. Manhole spacing (34.1): no more than 400 feet for sewers 15 inches and smaller, 500 feet for 18 to 30 inches, and up to 600 feet where modern cleaning equipment is available. Drop manhole (34.2): a drop pipe is needed when the incoming sewer is 24 inches or more above the manhole invert; under 24 inches the invert is filleted. Manhole size (34.3): at least 48 inches in diameter with a 24-inch minimum access opening. Alignment (33.5): sewers 24 inches and smaller are laid straight between manholes and checked by laser or lamping. Slope must be uniform between manholes (33.44). Velocities over 10 feet per second need protection against scour (33.45). Sewers on slopes of 20 percent or more are anchored: every 36 feet on 20 to 35 percent grades, 24 feet on 35 to 50 percent, 16 feet at 50 percent and steeper (33.46). Your state's own design rule and the project specs govern.
field.title: Ten States Standards for sewers: manhole spacing, drops, alignment, steep slopes (Chapter 30)
field.topic: Sewer design standards: slopes, manholes, sizes
field.source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition). Leakage tests (33.9): by water, leakage in or out must not exceed 100 gallons per inch of pipe diameter per mile per day, tested with at least 2 feet of positive head (33.94); by air, follow ASTM C828 for clay pipe, ASTM C924 for concrete pipe and ASTM F1417 for plastic pipe (33.95). Deflection test (33.85): required for all flexible pipe, run after the final backfill has been in place at least 30 days; no pipe may exceed 5 percent deflection; the rigid ball or mandrel is at least 95 percent of the pipe's base or average inside diameter and is pulled by hand, with no mechanical pulling devices. Manholes (34.7): inspected and tested for watertightness before going into service; air (vacuum) testing of concrete manholes follows ASTM C1244. Project specs are often tighter than these numbers, so read the testing section of your contract.
field.title: Ten States Standards sewer tests: 100 gallon leakage limit, air test standards, 5 percent deflection, manhole test
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Section 38, protection of water supplies). Side by side (38.31): sewers are laid at least 10 feet horizontally from any existing or proposed water main, measured edge to edge. Where 10 feet is not practical the reviewing agency can allow closer on a case-by-case basis if the water main is in a separate trench, or on an undisturbed earth shelf at one side of the sewer trench, with the bottom of the water main at least 18 inches above the top of the sewer. If neither can be done, both lines are built of slip-on or mechanical joint pipe rated at least 150 psi and pressure tested. Crossings (38.32): at least 18 inches between the outside of the water main and the outside of the sewer, whether the water main is above or below; keep sewer joints as far as possible from water main joints. If 18 inches cannot be met, either build the sewer to water pipe standards and pressure test it, or encase the water main or the sewer in a watertight carrier pipe that extends 10 feet on both sides of the crossing. State rules vary: check the state's own separation rule.
field.title: Ten States Standards: sewer and water main separation, 10 feet and 18 inches (Section 38)
field.topic: Water and sewer separation distances
field.source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Montana (DEQ Circular DEQ-1, Standards for Water Works, 2022 edition, Chapter 8). Pressure (8.2.1): at least 35 psi normal working pressure and at least 20 psi under all flow conditions; normal working pressure should be about 60 to 80 psi. Size (8.2.2): mains serving fire hydrants are at least 6 inches; at least 3 inches where there is no fire protection. Hydrants (8.4): 6-inch lead; hydrant drains may not connect to, or be within 10 feet of, sanitary sewers or storm drains. Installation (8.7): continuous uniform bedding; enough cover to prevent freezing; pressure and leakage tests per the AWWA standards; flushing, disinfection and bacteria testing per AWWA C651. Separation from sewers (8.8): at least 10 feet horizontal, edge to edge, from gravity sanitary or storm sewers (8.8.2); at least 18 inches vertical at crossings, outside to outside (8.8.3), with reduced crossings down to 6 inches only under listed conditions such as a 150 psi tested sewer and encasement or flowable fill 10 feet each side; force mains 10 feet horizontal and 18 inches vertical (8.8.4); no water pipe through or touching a sewer manhole, and mains should be at least 10 feet from manholes (8.8.5).
field.title: Montana water main rules: pressure, hydrants, sewer separation (Circular DEQ-1, Chapter 8)
field.topic: Spec books: water main installation, pressure test and disinfection
field.source: Montana DEQ Circular DEQ-1, Standards for Water Works, 2022 edition, Chapter 8 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Ductile iron pipe joints, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe (revised May 2015). Mechanical joint bolt torque (Table 4): 5/8 inch bolts on 3 inch joints 45 to 60 ft-lb; 3/4 inch bolts on 4 to 24 inch 75 to 90 ft-lb; 1 inch bolts on 30 to 36 inch 100 to 120 ft-lb; 1-1/4 inch bolts on 42 to 48 inch 120 to 150 ft-lb. Tighten in a star pattern and go around again until every bolt is in range. Push-on joints: clean the bell groove and the spigot, seat the gasket, lubricate the gasket and the plain end (not the socket), bevel field cuts, push straight home and deflect only after the joint is made. Maximum push-on deflection on an 18-foot length (Table 5): 5 degrees, about 19 inches of offset, for 3 to 12 inch; 3 degrees, about 11 inches, for 14 to 42 inch. Mechanical joints (Table 6): 6 inch 7 degrees (27 inches); 8 to 12 inch 5 degrees (20 inches); 14 inch 3.5 degrees; 24 inch about 2 degrees. Cutting: abrasive saw (about a minute per inch of diameter), then grind and bevel the end. Check the pipe maker's own table for the exact joint: restrained joints allow less.
field.title: Ductile iron pipe joints: mechanical joint bolt torque and maximum joint deflection (DIPRA guide)
field.topic: Pipe installation guides by material
field.source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Testing a new ductile iron water main, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide (revised May 2015), which follows AWWA C600 and C651. Pressure test: at least 1.5 times the working pressure at the lowest point of the section, held for at least 2 hours (150 psi working means a 225 psi test). Measure the make-up water needed to hold pressure; examples of the testing allowance at 150 psi are about 0.50 gallon per hour per 1,000 feet of 6 inch and 0.99 for 12 inch. Brace or restrain temporary plugs and caps. Flush at 3.0 feet per second: roughly 400 gpm for a 6 inch main and 1,060 gpm for a 12 inch. Chlorination (AWWA C651): tablet method, granules at the start and every 500 feet and 5-gram tablets at joints, fill slowly at 1 foot per second or less, hold 24 hours (48 hours if the water is colder than 41 F), about 25 mg/L; continuous feed, at least 25 mg/L going in and at least 10 mg/L left after 24 hours; slug method, at least 100 mg/L for at least 3 hours, start over if it drops below 50 mg/L. Flush the strong chlorine out within about a day, dechlorinate where the discharge rule requires it, then take bacteria samples. The water agency's spec governs.
field.title: Water main pressure test, flushing and chlorination basics (DIPRA guide, AWWA C600 and C651)
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Thrust restraint basics, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe (revised May 2015). Water pressure pushes on every bend, tee, reducer, valve and dead end. Example thrust at 100 psi: a 12 inch 90 degree bend pushes about 19,353 lb and a 12 inch dead end about 13,685 lb; thrust scales straight with pressure, so use test pressure, not working pressure. Example soil bearing values at 4 feet deep (Table 8): muck 0, sand about 4,000 lb per square foot, hard clay about 9,000. Common practice is block bearing area = thrust divided by the allowable soil bearing, poured against undisturbed soil. Blocks are concrete of at least 2,000 psi, cured at least five days before testing. Mechanical joints by themselves hold no thrust. Restrained joints (or wedge-action glands) are used instead of blocks where space is tight or the soil behind the block may be dug out later; the restrained length comes from the engineer or the agency table. Always build what the plans or the agency thrust block detail shows; these numbers are examples, not a design.
field.title: Thrust blocks at bends and dead ends: forces, soil bearing values, how strong the concrete (DIPRA guide)
field.topic: Thrust blocks and restrained joints
field.source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Corrugated HDPE storm pipe cover, summarized from ADS Technical Note TN 2.01 (rev. AB, 2024) for N-12 pipe. Minimum cover under H-20, H-25 or HL-93 traffic: 1 foot over the crown for 4 to 48 inch pipe and 2 feet for 54 and 60 inch; flexible pavement thickness does not count toward it, and construction or paving equipment may need more temporary cover (see the ADS Drainage Handbook installation section). Maximum cover depends on the backfill around the pipe. Examples in feet for 12 / 24 / 36 / 48 / 60 inch: Class 1 compacted stone 35 / 28 / 26 / 25 / 25; Class 2 at 95 percent 24 / 20 / 18 / 17 / 17; Class 2 at 90 percent 17 / 13 / 12 / 11 / 11; Class 2 at 85 percent 8 / 7 / 7 / 7 / 6; Class 3 at 95 percent 17 / 14 / 13 / 12 / 12; Class 3 at 90 percent 11 / 10 / 9 / 7 / 7. The table assumes installation per ASTM D2321, no groundwater pressure and 120 pcf soil. These are general guidance, not a project design, and other makers' pipe has its own tables.
field.title: ADS N-12 corrugated HDPE pipe: minimum and maximum cover (TN 2.01)
field.topic: Pipe cover: minimum and maximum burial depth
field.source: ADS (Advanced Drainage Systems) Technical Note TN 2.01, Minimum and Maximum Burial Depth for Corrugated HDPE Pipe (per AASHTO), rev. AB, copyright 2024 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Testing concrete sewer and storm pipe, summarized from the American Concrete Pipe Association installation manual. Infiltration test: only meaningful when groundwater is at least 2 feet over the crown; the manual's base allowance is 200 gallons per inch of diameter per mile per day at 6 feet of head, rising to 282 at 12 feet. Exfiltration test: base head 3 feet; single reaches can run over if the project average passes. Low-pressure air test follows ASTM C924 and is limited to pipe 24 inch and smaller; it finds construction defects but does not measure water leakage. Larger pipe is tested one joint at a time with air or water under ASTM C1103. Vacuum testing: ASTM C1214 for pipe 4 to 36 inch, ASTM C1244 for manholes. Visual inspection looks for debris, cracks, joints fully home and sealed, smooth inverts and properly set frames. The project spec sets the pass numbers; many agencies allow far less leakage than 200 gallons (the Ten States figure is 100).
field.title: Concrete pipe acceptance tests: infiltration, exfiltration, air, joint and vacuum tests (ACPA)
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: American Concrete Pipe Association, Concrete Pipe and Box Culvert Installation manual (our summary; read 2026-11-20). Standard Installations are the ones in ASTM C1479 and ASCE 15.

field.text: Vitrified clay pipe is installed under ASTM C12. Clay is rigid pipe, so the bedding class sets how much load the pipe can carry: the pipe's bearing strength is multiplied by the bedding load factor. Load factors published by the National Clay Pipe Institute from ASTM C12: Class D (flat trench bottom, least support) 1.1; Class C 1.5; Class B 1.9; crushed stone encasement 2.2; controlled low-strength material (CLSM, flowable fill) 2.8; concrete cradle 3.4. The plans call out the class; a crew that builds Class C where Class B was designed has cut the pipe's safe load by about a fifth. Shape bell holes so the barrel, not the bell, carries the load, and haunch the pipe by shovel slicing. Ten States Standards (33.83) point to these same ASTM C12 classes for rigid sewer pipe.
field.title: Clay pipe (VCP) bedding classes and load factors, ASTM C12
field.topic: Pipe installation guides by material
field.source: National Clay Pipe Institute bedding sheet (2021), load factors from ASTM C12, Standard Practice for Installing Vitrified Clay Pipe Lines (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Georgia (GDOT Section 550, Storm Drain Pipe, Pipe-Arch Culverts, and Side Drain Pipe, supplemental specification revised 2015). Foundation and backfill follow Section 207 and Georgia Standards 1030D and 1030P. Thermoplastic pipe outside the roadbed in fills up to 10 feet uses Class II B2 or better soil for HDPE and Class II B3 or better for PVC and polypropylene; above 10 feet, graded aggregate (550.3.03). Thermoplastic joints are at least silt tight (550.3.05.C). Post-installation inspection (550.3.06): once compacted backfill reaches 8 feet or final cover is complete, with at least seven days notice to the Engineer; low-distortion video with laser profiling of 100 percent of storm drain pipe and at least 10 percent of side drain pipe on state route projects, by NASSCO PACP certified operators; manual inspection is allowed in pipe over 48 inches. Deflection over 5 percent of nominal diameter needs an evaluation by a Professional Engineer; over 7.5 percent is remediated or replaced. Joint separation over 1 inch must be fixed. Lift thickness and compaction percent are not confirmed here (they are not in Section 550); see Section 207.
field.title: Georgia GDOT storm drain pipe: video and laser inspection, 5 and 7.5 percent deflection (Section 550)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Georgia DOT Supplemental Specification Section 550, Storm Drain Pipe, Pipe-Arch Culverts, and Side Drain Pipe (revised 2015; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Kentucky (KYTC Standard Specifications, Section 701, culvert pipe, entrance pipe and storm sewer pipe). Bedding: No. 8 or No. 9-M stone or fine aggregate; do not use DGA or gravel base (701.02.04). Backfill in 6-inch lifts compacted to not less than 95 percent of maximum density by Kentucky Method KM 64-511 (701.03.06). Keep construction equipment and traffic off the pipe until there is 48 inches of cover over it (701.03.07). Joints are soil tight and wrapped with geotextile; concrete pipe joints may be mortar (1 cement to 2 sand), asphalt mastic, rubber gaskets or butyl sealant, with tied joints within 12 feet of the outlet on slopes 3:1 or steeper; metal pipe bands are at least 12 inches wide for pipe 54 inches and smaller; thermoplastic pipe uses bell and spigot with elastomeric seals (701.03.05). Trench limits are on the Standard Drawings.
field.title: Kentucky KYTC culvert and storm sewer pipe: bedding, 6-inch lifts, 95 percent, 48 inches cover (Section 701)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Division 700, Sections 701, 705, 706, as posted by KYTC (edition year not shown in the file; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Kentucky (KYTC Standard Specifications, Section 705, pipeline inspection). Installed pipe gets a camera inspection under Kentucky Method KM 64-114, with at least 24 hours notice to the Engineer, 30 days or more after earthwork is complete to within 1 foot of finished subgrade (705.02). Flexible pipe up to 48 inches can be checked with a mandrel that has at least 9 legs (705.03). Deflection table (705.05): 0 to 5.0 percent, full payment; 5.1 to 9.9 percent, 50 percent payment; 10 percent or greater, remove and replace. Section 706, boring and jacking: access pits on both sides, guide rails kept to line and grade, casing fitted tight to the bore with continuous welds. Minimum steel casing wall: 0.375 inch for 18 inch and smaller, 0.500 inch for 24 to 30 inch, 0.532 inch for 36 inch, 0.625 inch for 42 inch (706.02.01).
field.title: Kentucky KYTC pipeline camera inspection, mandrel and deflection pay cuts (Section 705); boring and jacking (706)
field.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
field.source: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Division 700, Sections 701, 705, 706, as posted by KYTC (edition year not shown in the file; read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Iowa (Iowa DOT Standard Specifications, Section 2417, Corrugated Culverts, online version revised 10/20/2026). Corrugated metal or polyethylene roadway culverts get Class B bedding as shown in the contract documents (2417.03.C.1). Minimum cover: 1 foot over entrance culverts and 2 feet over roadway culverts; if construction traffic will cross, roadway culvert cover goes up to the pipe's nominal diameter or 3 feet, whichever is greater (2417.03.B). Polyethylene pipe deflection test (2417.03.C.2): at least 10 percent of locations, no sooner than 30 calendar days after backfill and before paving; the inside diameter may not shrink more than 5.0 percent; pipe 30 inches and smaller is tested with a nine-point mandrel, larger pipe is checked along its whole length. City street and utility work in Iowa usually follows SUDAS instead of the DOT book.
field.title: Iowa DOT corrugated metal and plastic culverts: cover and the 5 percent deflection test (Section 2417)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Iowa DOT Standard Specifications (current online General Supplemental series, page revised 10/20/2026), Section 2417 Corrugated Culverts (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Montana (MDT Standard Specifications, 2025 book, Section 603, Culverts, Storm Drains, Sanitary Sewers). Bedding is placed per Section 207 and the Detailed Drawings, with material tamped firmly under the pipe haunches (603.03.2, 603.04.3(B)). Backfill goes in layers of 6 inches loose thickness or less, to the moisture and density required by Subsection 203.03.3 (the percent is set there, not in 603). Heavy equipment stays off until cover is at least 4 feet or one-half the pipe diameter, whichever is greater (603.03.4(A)). Round concrete pipe joints are watertight with rubber gaskets (603.03.3(A)); siphon and irrigation pipe get a water-tightness test (MT 420); manhole connections follow ASTM C923. Section 604, manholes and inlets: backfill in loose layers of 6 inches or less, foundation compacted for full bearing.
field.title: Montana MDT culverts, storm drains and sewers: 6-inch lifts and 4 feet of cover before heavy equipment (Section 603)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Montana DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025 redline book, Sections 603 and 604 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Wyoming (WYDOT 2021 Standard Specifications, Section 206, Excavation and Backfill for Culverts). Backfill in loose layers of about 8 inches, each compacted to at least 95.0 percent of maximum density at moisture between plus 2 and minus 4 percent of optimum (206.4.5.1). Compact the last 6 inches below structures or bedding to at least 95.0 percent (206.4.4). Over water and sewer lines, hand-place the first 12 inches. Do not backfill against cast-in-place boxes until 14 calendar days or 80 percent of design strength. Flowable fill: at least 12 inches over the conduit and no vehicle loads until 24 hours after it sets (206.4.5.3). Pipe bedding and laying are in Section 603 (603.4.4 and 603.4.5). Section 212, structure backfill: loose layers of about 8 inches compacted to the density of the adjacent material, placed evenly on both sides.
field.title: Wyoming WYDOT culvert excavation and backfill: 8-inch lifts at 95 percent (Section 206)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: Wyoming DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2021 edition, Sections 206 and 212 (read 2026-11-20; Section 603 not read)

field.text: Arizona (ADOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). Edition: the 2021 edition is in use now; ADOT says the 2027 edition applies to all projects advertising on and after January 4, 2027, electronic only, so check which book your contract names. Section 501, Pipe Culvert and Storm Drains, as described in ADOT's own Construction Manual (March 2025): a written trenching plan is required for trenches deeper than 5 feet (501-1); trench widths and the minimum 1 foot of cover are on Standard Drawing C-13.15, and cover must be increased for construction traffic, which is the contractor's responsibility (501-3.01); pipe 36 inches and larger in a trench is bedded in cement-treated slurry from the trench bottom to the springline (501-3.04); replacement backfill is compacted to 95 percent of maximum density (501-3.07(B)). The manual advises inspectors that heavy vibratory equipment should not run directly over pipe until there is at least 3 feet of cover and that nothing should be placed on flowable fill for 24 hours. In the Phoenix area, city and county work usually follows the MAG Uniform Standard Specifications instead.
field.title: Arizona ADOT pipe culverts and storm drains (Section 501) and the 2027 spec book change
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: ADOT Construction Manual, Chapter 5, Sections 501-505 (March 2025), describing the ADOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction; edition notice at azdot.gov/business/contracts-and-specifications (both read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas, City of Fort Worth (Standard Specification 33 05 10, Utility Trench Excavation, Embedment and Backfill, revised April 2, 2021). Embedment and initial backfill go 6 to 12 inches above the pipe for water lines and for sanitary sewer and HDPE storm pipe; reinforced concrete storm pipe is embedded to the spring line; polypropylene storm pipe gets crushed rock to the top of pipe (3.4.D). Embedment and initial backfill are compacted to 95 percent Standard Proctor (ASTM D698). Final backfill: loose lifts of 12 inches or less; 95 percent under existing or future pavement less than 15 feet deep, 98 percent for select fill 15 feet and deeper, 95 percent outside pavement; moisture from minus 2 to plus 5 percent of optimum (3.4.E.3). Density tests: at least one per 2 vertical feet of compacted backfill and at least every 200 feet of trench, staggered by lift (3.7.A.2.d). Water lines 12 inch and smaller: top of pipe at least 42 inches below proposed grade unless the drawings say otherwise. Trench safety follows OSHA Subpart P and an Excavation Safety Plan designed by a Texas-licensed engineer. Other cities in the area use the NCTCOG specifications.
field.title: Texas, Fort Worth utility trench spec: embedment, 12-inch lifts, 95 and 98 percent, test frequency (33 05 10)
field.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
field.source: City of Fort Worth Standard Specification 33 05 10, Utility Trench Excavation, Embedment and Backfill, revised April 2, 2021 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Texas uses 9 feet, not 10. TCEQ rules: sewer pipe and manholes should be at least 9 feet from water lines, in a separate trench and below the water line where possible (30 TAC 217.53(d); 30 TAC 290.44(e)(1)). When 9 feet cannot be met, parallel lines: the water line at least 2 feet above and 4 feet to the side of the sewer, with 150 psi pressure-rated sewer pipe, or encasement (217.53(d)(6); 290.44(e)(4)(A)). Sewer crossing under a water line: 150 psi pipe with at least 6 inches of separation, one length at least 18 feet long centered on the water line; or other pipe with at least 2 feet of separation and cement-stabilized sand; or a casing pipe at least two sizes larger with spacers no more than 5 feet apart (217.53(d)(7)). A manhole within 9 feet of a water line must pass the leak test or get at least 1 foot of cement-stabilized sand. Water lines: at least 24 inches of cover, 35 psi minimum pressure, fire hydrants not within 9 feet of sewer lines, new mains disinfected per AWWA C651 with at least one bacteria sample per 1,000 feet (290.44).
field.title: Texas water and sewer separation: the 9-foot rule (TCEQ 30 TAC 217.53 and 290.44)
field.topic: Water and sewer separation distances
field.source: 30 Texas Administrative Code 217.53 (TCEQ, wastewater collection pipe design; amended eff. 12/4/2015) and 30 TAC 290.44 (water distribution), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-11-20

field.text: Florida has its own separation numbers (F.A.C. Rule 62-555.314, amended effective 2/26/2025). Side by side, a new or relocated water main is at least: 3 feet from storm sewers, stormwater force mains and regulated reclaimed water lines; 3 feet, preferably 10, from vacuum sanitary sewers; 6 feet, preferably 10, from gravity or pressure sanitary sewers and wastewater force mains (gravity sewer can come down to 3 feet if the bottom of the water main is at least 6 inches above the top of the sewer); 10 feet from onsite sewage (septic) systems. Crossing a gravity or vacuum sewer or storm sewer: water main at least 6 inches, preferably 12, above, or at least 12 inches below; above is preferred. Crossing a pressure sewer, force main or reclaimed line: at least 12 inches above or below. At crossings, center one full length of water main, or keep water main joints at least 3 feet from storm and vacuum sewer joints and 6 feet from sanitary sewer and force main joints. No water main may pass through or touch a sanitary sewer manhole. The Department can allow exceptions with extra protection such as pressure-rated sewer pipe, a casing or concrete encasement.
field.title: Florida water main separation from sewer, storm and reclaimed lines (Rule 62-555.314)
field.topic: Water and sewer separation distances
field.source: Florida Administrative Code Rule 62-555.314, Location of Public Water System Mains (amended eff. 2/26/2025), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-11-20

field.text: Florida (FDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). FDOT publishes a new eBook each fiscal year: the FY 2026-27 book took effect July 1, 2026 and the FY 2027-28 book takes effect July 1, 2027; your contract names the one that applies. The sections a pipe crew lives in are Section 125 (Excavation for Structures and Pipe), Section 430 (Pipe Culverts) and Section 425 (Inlets, Manholes, and Junction Boxes), with jack and bore in Section 556. The numbers in those sections are not confirmed in this library (the files would not open here), so for lift thickness, density and pipe inspection go to the book itself at fdot.gov/specifications. County and city utility work in Florida usually follows the utility's own standards, and water main separation follows state Rule 62-555.314.
field.title: Florida FDOT Standard Specifications: which edition is in force (July-to-June books)
field.topic: Spec books: which edition applies
field.source: FDOT Standard Specification Library, fdot.gov/specifications/standard-specification-library (edition list read 2026-11-20); section numbers not re-read

field.text: Indiana (INDOT Standard Specifications Section 715, Pipe Culverts, and Storm and Sanitary Sewers, as changed by Recurring Special Provision 715-R-809 dated 09-01-26). After the visual or video inspection, plastic pipe is mandrel tested: corrugated and smooth-wall polyethylene, corrugated polypropylene, and profile and smooth-wall PVC. The Engineer picks the runs, and at least 10 percent of the total length of each material is tested; underdrain pipe is exempt. Backfill for corrugated pipe may not have particles larger than half the corrugation depth. Thermoplastic and metal pipe must come from INDOT's qualified products list. The deflection limit, lift thickness and compaction numbers are in the base Section 715 and Section 211 text, which was not read here, so those numbers are not confirmed.
field.title: Indiana INDOT pipe: mandrel testing of plastic pipe, Section 715
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: INDOT Recurring Special Provision 715-R-809, Pipe Culverts, and Storm and Sanitary Sewers, dated 09-01-26 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: North Dakota (NDDOT 2023 Standard Specifications, Section 714, Culverts, Storm Drains, Edgedrains, and Underdrains). Bedding is tamped under both haunches up to 15 percent of the pipe height with hand-held air tampers (714.04 A.4). Backfill in lifts of 6 inches or less; aggregate backfill compacted to at least 90 percent of maximum dry density at 2 points below to 3 points above optimum moisture (714.04 A.10 and A.11). Cover before equipment crosses: the book gives no number and sends you to the pipe maker's recommendation (714.04 A.12). Deflection test: metal and thermoplastic pipe under mainline and paved crossroads is tested at least 30 days after installation with a nine-point mandrel at least 95 percent of the inside diameter; pipe the mandrel will not pass is replaced (714.04 A.8). Concrete pipe joints are wrapped in geotextile. Jacked steel pipe: bore without water, start within 0.1 foot of staked grade, and stay within 1/2 foot of line and grade (714.04 C). Manholes and inlets (722): backfill lifts of 6 inches or less at 90 percent. Water and sewer lines (724): bedding up the sides to one-third of the pipe diameter, backfill in 6-inch loose lifts.
field.title: North Dakota NDDOT culverts and storm drains: 6-inch lifts, 90 percent, 95 percent mandrel (Section 714)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: North Dakota DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2023, Sections 714, 722, 724 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: Ohio (ODOT Construction and Material Specifications, Item 611, Pipe Culverts, Sewers, Drains, and Drainage Structures). These numbers are from the 2013 online edition; the current 2023 book was not checked, so treat them as not confirmed for a current job and read Item 611 in the contract's edition. In Item 611 the contractor's installation plan sets trench dimensions, bedding, lift thickness and compaction (611.04, 611.06); rock or unsuitable material is removed at least 6 inches below the pipe and replaced with structural backfill; if no bedding is used, the middle third of the bed is loosened. With low-strength mortar bedding, the mortar backfill is carried at least 6 inches over the conduit. Performance inspection (611.12): for runs over 20 feet, 30 to 90 days after finished grade, with 5 workdays notice to the Engineer and a video record. Metal and plastic conduit is repaired or replaced if the mandrel will not pass or the laser profile shows more than 7.5 percent deflection (611.13). Sanitary concrete pipe joints are tested under ASTM C969 or C1103. Structure inverts must be within 0.1 foot or 5 percent of the pipe diameter, whichever is greater (611.14).
field.title: Ohio ODOT pipe culverts and sewers: installation plan, 7.5 percent deflection, 30 to 90 day inspection (Item 611)
field.topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
field.source: Ohio DOT Construction and Material Specifications, Item 611, 2013 online edition (read 2026-11-20). The current book is the 2023 C&MS with yearly updates, which was not read.

field.text: Nevada (NDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). NDOT lists the 2024 edition as current. The numbers for pipe culverts, structure excavation and backfill in the 2024 book are not confirmed in this library because the file would not open; get them from the book on NDOT's Standard Specifications and Plans page or from the NDOT Specifications office. In the Las Vegas valley, city, county and water district work normally follows the Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Clark County instead, and in the Reno area the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (the Orange Book), each with the agency's own amendments. Your contract says which book governs.

field.topic: Spec books: which edition applies
field.source: Nevada DOT, Standard Specifications, Standard Plans, and Design Guides page (edition list read 2026-11-20; the 2024 book itself would not open)

field.text: Utah (UDOT Standard Specifications). UDOT's standards page lists yearly books, with 2027 the newest listed above 2026 and 2025; the contract names the one that applies. The numbers in UDOT's drainage pipe and backfill sections are not confirmed in this library because the files would not open; read the section in the contract's edition on UDOT's standards page or ask the UDOT Standards Coordinator. City, county and district utility work along the Wasatch Front usually follows the APWA Utah Chapter Manual of Standard Specifications and Plans with local amendments, not the UDOT book.
field.title: Utah UDOT Standard Specifications: editions listed and where city work differs
field.topic: Spec books: which edition applies

field.text: Oregon (2024 Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction). This edition applies to ODOT projects bid on or after Dec. 1, 2023, and many cities use it with their own special provisions. Trench width at the surface is as narrow as practical but not less than 24 inches (00405.41(c)); the pipe zone runs to at least 8 inches over the pipe (00405.02); trench backfill is 95 percent of AASHTO T 99 under roadway and shoulders and 90 percent elsewhere (00405.46(c)(2)). Video inspection: the camera moves no faster than 30 feet per minute while recording (00445.74). Deflection mandrel: at least 9 vanes, 95 percent of the pipe's initial inside diameter, not less than 30 days after backfill (00445.73(c)). Tunneling, boring and jacking (Section 00406): pipe, casing or sleeves are jacked or bored to the required line and grade, and jacked casings 36 inches and larger get grout nipples at 10-foot centers when pressure grouting is specified (00406.12). Manhole vacuum test: 10 inches of mercury, timed to 9 inches (00470.71(b)). Adjusting structures (00490.46): no more than 24 inches from the new frame grade to the top of the cone.
field.title: Oregon ODOT 2024 book: effective date, video speed, boring and jacking, adjusting manholes
field.topic: Spec books: jacking, boring and tunneling
field.source: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction, 2024 (ODOT/APWA Oregon Chapter), Sections 00405, 00406, 00445, 00470, 00490 (read 2026-11-20)

field.text: A commercial driver license (CDL) is needed by weight rating, not by what the truck looks like (49 CFR 383.5). Class A (combination): the truck and trailer together are rated or weigh 26,001 lb or more AND the trailer is rated or weighs more than 10,000 lb. Class B (heavy straight truck): the single truck is rated or weighs 26,001 lb or more, for example most tandem dump trucks and water trucks. Class C: smaller vehicles built for 16 or more people including the driver, or hauling placarded hazardous materials. The rule uses whichever is greater, the rating on the door tag (GVWR) or the real weight. The combination rating (GCWR) is the greater of the maker's number on the power unit's label or the truck GVWR plus the trailer GVWR. Worked example: a pickup tagged 14,000 lb GVWR pulling an equipment trailer tagged 14,000 lb is 28,000 lb combined with a trailer over 10,000 lb, so it is a Class A combination. The same pickup with a 9,900 lb trailer is 23,900 lb and needs no CDL. A 25,999 lb straight truck with a trailer of 10,000 lb or less needs no CDL either. States issue the license and may add their own rules, and some state exemptions exist, so check the state driver manual.
field.title: When a crew truck needs a CDL: the 26,001 lb and 10,000 lb trailer rule (Class A, B, C)
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.source: 49 CFR 383.5 (definitions: commercial motor vehicle Groups A, B, C; GCWR; GVWR)
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20

field.text: Two federal weight lines get mixed up. 26,001 lb is the CDL line. 10,001 lb is the "commercial motor vehicle" line for the safety rules. 49 CFR 390.5 says a commercial motor vehicle is a vehicle "used on a highway in interstate commerce to transport passengers or property" that has a "gross vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating, or gross vehicle weight or gross combination weight, of 4,536 kg (10,001 pounds) or more, whichever is greater". So a 1 ton pickup pulling a mini excavator is usually over 10,001 lb combined, with no CDL needed. Above that line the driver and truck come under the federal motor carrier safety rules that use this definition: a medical card (49 CFR 391.45), hours of service (Part 395), load checks (392.9), daily defect reports and a yearly inspection (Part 396), and a USDOT number on the truck. These are the federal (interstate) rules. A truck that never leaves the state follows that state's version, usually close: check with the state.
field.title: The 10,001 lb line: when a pickup and trailer becomes a DOT commercial vehicle (no CDL needed)
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.source: 49 CFR 390.5 (definition of commercial motor vehicle, 10,001 lb); 49 CFR 383.5 (26,001 lb CDL line)
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20

field.text: FMCSA says a company needs a USDOT number when it runs a vehicle in interstate commerce that has a weight rating or weight "of 4,536 kg (10,001 pounds) or more, whichever is greater" (truck alone or truck plus trailer), or carries placarded hazardous materials. Interstate means trade that crosses a state line, "Between a place in a State and a place outside of such State". For companies that stay inside one state, FMCSA lists the states that also require a USDOT number for in-state commercial trucks: AL, AK, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, ID, IN, IA, KS, KY, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, MT, NE, NV, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, WA, WV, WI, WY, plus Puerto Rico. Each of those states sets its own weight line for in-state trucks, so check with the state. A state not on the list may still have its own state number or permit. The number is free from FMCSA and is tied to the company, not to each truck. The list is from the FMCSA page as updated September 3, 2025.
field.title: Do we need a DOT number (USDOT number) on our pickups and work trucks, even if we only work in state
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.source: FMCSA, "Do I Need a USDOT Number?" (page updated 2025-09-03); 49 CFR 390.5
field.edition: FMCSA web page, last updated September 3, 2025

field.text: A driver of a commercial motor vehicle (10,001 lb or more in interstate commerce, with or without a CDL) must be medically examined and certified by a medical examiner. 49 CFR 391.45 requires a new exam for any driver who has not been certified "during the preceding 24 months". Some drivers are on a 12 month cycle instead: drivers with insulin-treated diabetes, drivers certified under the alternative vision standard, and drivers in an exempt intracity zone. A driver whose ability to do the job has been affected by an injury or illness must be examined again before driving, whatever the date on the card. A medical examiner can also write a card for less than 24 months to watch a condition such as high blood pressure. So the pipelayer who only drives the 1 ton with the equipment trailer needs a current medical card, not just the CDL drivers. These are the federal (interstate) rules. A truck that never leaves the state follows that state's version, usually close: check with the state.
field.title: DOT medical card: who needs one and how often (every 24 months)
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.source: 49 CFR 391.45 (persons who must be medically examined and certified); 49 CFR 390.5
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20

field.text: Federal hours of service for property-carrying commercial trucks (49 CFR 395.3): 10 hours off first: "A driver may not drive without first taking 10 consecutive hours off duty". 14 hour window: a driver may not drive after 14 consecutive hours from coming on duty. Breaks do not stop that clock. 11 hours driving: "A driver may drive a total of 11 hours" inside the 14 hour window. 30 minute break: no driving once more than 8 hours of driving time have passed without at least a 30 minute interruption (off duty, or on duty not driving). Short-haul drivers are excused. Weekly: no driving after 60 hours on duty in 7 days (company does not run every day) or 70 hours in 8 days (company runs every day). Restart: 34 or more consecutive hours off duty resets the 7 or 8 day count. Unexpected bad weather or traffic allows up to 2 more hours (395.1(b)(1)). The limits stop the driving, not the work. These are the federal (interstate) rules. A truck that never leaves the state follows that state's version, usually close: check with the state.
field.title: Hours of service for truck drivers: 11 hours driving, 14 hour day, 30 minute break, 60/70 hours
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20

field.text: Most pipe crews need no logbook because of the short-haul exception, 49 CFR 395.1(e). CDL drivers, 395.1(e)(1): no log is needed on a day when the driver stays "within a 150 air-mile radius (172.6 statute miles) of the normal work reporting location", returns there and is released within 14 consecutive hours, and has at least 10 hours off before the next shift. Drivers of trucks that do not need a CDL, 395.1(e)(2): stay within 150 air miles and return to the normal reporting location at the end of each shift; they may not drive after the 14th hour on duty on 5 days of any 7, and may go to the 16th hour on 2 days of the 7. The company keeps time records for 6 months (time in, time out, total hours each day). The 11 hour driving limit and the 60/70 hour weekly limits still apply. On a day the driver goes past the radius or the hours, a regular log is required. These are the federal (interstate) rules. A truck that never leaves the state follows that state's version, usually close: check with the state.
field.title: Short-haul exception: no logbook inside 150 air miles (time cards instead)
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20

field.text: Two federal hours-of-service exceptions are written for our kind of work. Construction materials and equipment, 49 CFR 395.1(m): for a driver mainly hauling construction materials and equipment, "any period of 7 or 8 consecutive days may end with the beginning of any off-duty period of 24 or more successive hours." So the weekly 60 or 70 hour count restarts after 24 hours off instead of 34. The definition (395.2) covers hauling "to or from an active construction site" "within a 75 air mile radius of the normal work reporting location of the driver"; a state may set 50 to 75 air miles for in-state moves. Utility service vehicles, 395.1(n): the hours-of-service part does not apply at all to drivers of a utility service vehicle, which 395.2 defines as a commercial vehicle used to repair, maintain or operate utility facilities and "operated primarily within the service area of a utility's subscribers or consumers". That fits a utility's own service trucks and contractors doing that repair and maintenance work; whether a truck on new-construction pipe work qualifies is not confirmed here, so ask the state DOT enforcement office before relying on it.
field.title: Construction and utility truck exceptions to hours of service: the 24 hour restart
field.topic: DOT rules for crew trucks: CDL, medical card, hours of service, inspections, loads
field.source: 49 CFR 395.1(m), 395.1(n); 49 CFR 395.2 (definitions)
field.edition: eCFR text as shown on law.cornell.edu, read 2026-11-20
field.unconfirmed: whether new-construction pipe crews fit the utility service vehicle definition

field.text: Yes. For a worker who also drives a commercial truck (10,001 lb or more), time spent working in the trench counts as on-duty time. 49 CFR 395.2 says on-duty time "means all time from the time a driver begins to work or is required to be in readiness to work" until relieved. It includes driving, servicing the truck, loading, and "any other work for a motor carrier". The 14 hour rule in 395.3 says a driver may not drive after 14 consecutive hours from coming on duty. Put together: a pipelayer who clocks in at 6:00 am, lays pipe all day, and is still on the job at 8:00 pm cannot legally drive the equipment truck and trailer back to the yard, unless the 16 hour short-haul day for non-CDL trucks applies (allowed on 2 days in 7, see 395.1(e)(2)). Someone inside their hours has to drive, or the truck stays. The weekly 60 or 70 hour count includes the trench hours too. These are the federal (interstate) rules.
